# 0. Purpose

This notebook runs the robustness checks for Study 1. Most of them change
one analytic choice, or a set of choices, and report what happens to the
estimates the paper rests on; the power analyses of section 4 ask instead
what the design could have detected. The notebook runs last in the Study 1
pipeline, after `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd`, `Study1_02_Text.ipynb` and
`Study1_03_Integration.Rmd` have produced their outputs.

Contents:

1. **Bayesian replication** of the primary LMMs (linear mixed models:
   regressions that give each participant and each image its own baseline)
   in `brms`, which fits the same kind of model by posterior sampling. The
   priors are weakly informative, wide enough that the data and not the
   prior set the estimates, and posterior predictive checks plot ratings
   simulated from each fitted model over the observed ratings.
2. **Equivalence sensitivity at the wider bounds.** H3 predicts that the
   attribution penalty is the same size for figurative and non-figurative
   images. Its registered equivalence test is run in `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd`
   section 7.10, beside the model whose term it tests, at the registered
   bound of ±0.20 rating points. Two random-effects structures are used:
   intercepts only (a baseline per participant and per image) and maximal
   (which adds the random slopes the design allows, letting an effect vary
   from one participant or image to the next). This notebook runs the
   descriptive sensitivity the preregistration asks for alongside it. Here
   the two one-sided tests (one against each end of the bound) are run at
   the wider bounds of 0.30 and 0.50 rating points, beside the Bayesian
   version of the same question, a region of practical equivalence (the
   share of the posterior that falls inside the bound). These rows carry no
   verdict on H3.
3. **Sensitivity power analysis** with `simr::powerSim`, which simulates
   new datasets from a fitted model and counts how often a term is
   detected. The design is held as fitted: the realized N, and the variances
   the model attributes to participants, to images and to the remainder.
   One coefficient is FIXED at a series of hypothesized values, and the
   question is the smallest coefficient, in rating units, that the design
   detects with 80% power. This is design sensitivity, not observed or
   post-hoc power (power computed at the effect the data happened to show).
   For H1 (the attribution contrast defined below) the primary model is
   refitted with image kind sum-coded: the two kinds are coded +1 and -1, so
   that the other coefficients are read at the average of the two kinds
   rather than at the non-figurative kind. The fit itself is unchanged. Its
   `TypeAI` coefficient is the H1 contrast, so the hypothesized values are
   sizes of that contrast.
   The interaction term is included because H3 predicts no effect on it.
   The smallest interaction a significance test would detect is reported for
   H3 as descriptive context, and it carries no verdict, because detecting
   an effect and ruling out an effect of the bound's size are different
   questions. Whether the registered equivalence test for H3 is
   informative turns on the second question. Its answer is the power of the
   equivalence test itself: the probability that the 90 per cent interval
   on the interaction falls inside the registered bound when the true
   interaction is zero. Section 4 computes that power by simulation from the
   same fitted model, beside the detection power. It reads the power against
   the registered verdict and writes it, with the informativeness flag it
   governs, to `study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv`.
   Section 4.1 answers the H4 half of the same registered question by a
   simulation written out in full, at 55 and 56 participants per arm. Its
   main quantity is the spread of the between-participant variance-ratio
   estimate across simulated datasets: how far the estimate moves from one
   simulated sample of this size to the next, which is not the width or the
   coverage of any confidence interval. Beside it are the false-positive
   rate of the likelihood-ratio test (which compares the model with two
   between-participant variances against the model with one, by twice the
   difference in their log-likelihoods) when the arms share one variance,
   and the smallest ratio the design detects at 80% power.
4. **Covariate robustness**: refit the primary LMMs adding age, gender
   (collapsed to female, male and other) and art training or experience
   (scored 0 to 4) as fixed covariates. Race and language are not fitted.
   The H1 contrast should survive because of random assignment.
5. **Length-as-covariate**: add `n_words`, the word count of the
   justification, from the text measures. The justification is written
   after the rating, so length is a post-treatment variable (one the
   manipulation could itself have changed), and adjusting for it is a
   descriptive sensitivity check: it cannot rule out the "AI-condition
   participants just wrote less" objection. Section 6 compares length
   between the arms directly.
6. **Non-response / engagement** by condition. The survey forced a
   response to every open item, so what is tested here is response length:
   the primary models are refit without the participants whose median
   justification runs to fewer than three words.
7. **Stimulus-as-fixed sensitivity**: a refit that treats the ten images as
   fixed categories and drops the image random intercept (the per-image
   baseline the primary model treats as a draw from a population of
   images). Judd, Westfall and Kenny (2012) argue for the random treatment;
   this refit shows what the estimate does without it.
8. **Specification curve** (multiverse): the H1 contrast re-estimated under
   every distinct *effective* combination of reasonable analytic choices
   (covariates, random-effect structure, model family, aggregation level),
   where grid cells that lead to the same fit count once. The number
   reported is the number of distinct fits, not of grid cells. The curve is
   drawn separately for each scale: rating points, and the log-odds (the
   logarithm of the odds) of the CLMM, a cumulative link mixed model, which
   is an ordinal regression with random effects.

**One estimand for H1.** H1 is the attribution contrast that
`Study1_01_Quant.Rmd` tests: the mean rating under human attribution minus
the mean rating under generator attribution, averaged with equal weight over
the figurative and the non-figurative images. Every check below that
re-estimates H1 reports that one quantity, in a row labelled
`H1 contrast: Human - AI, averaged over image kind`. In a model that carries
the attribution-by-image-kind interaction, the regression coefficient
`TypeAI` is a different quantity. The models here use treatment coding, in
which each factor's first level (Human, non-figurative) is the baseline the
other coefficients are measured from. Under that coding `TypeAI` is the
generator-minus-human difference at the non-figurative images only, a simple
effect (the effect of one factor within a single level of the other). From
such a model the H1 contrast is computed with `emmeans`, the package that
averages a fitted model's predictions over the levels of the other factors to
give each arm's estimated marginal mean; the contrast is the difference
between the two arms. For the brms fits, emmeans does the same on every
posterior draw. In a model without the interaction, the coefficient is already
the attribution difference averaged over the ten images, five of each kind, so
the H1 contrast is that coefficient with its sign reversed, and the table says
so. Each estimate keeps its model's scale and is labelled with
it: rating points for the linear models, and log-odds, the scale of an
ordinal model's coefficients, for the ordinal ones. The `TypeAI` rows stay in
every table for comparison, labelled as simple effects, and section 8.2
collects the H1 contrast from every check in one table.

**Run record.** At the start of a run the notebook deletes every file it is
about to write, so that a section that fails or is skipped cannot leave an
older table in its place. Each model fit receives one of four statuses. `ok`
is a fit with no problem. `singular` is a fit that converged on the boundary
of its parameter space (a variance estimated at zero, or a correlation at
plus or minus one): the random-effects structure is richer than the data
support, and the estimates remain usable. `not_converged` is a fit for which
the optimizer or the sampler reported a failure; its test statistics,
p-values, intervals and readings are written as NA. `error` is a fit that
did not run. Section 9 writes `tables/study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv`. It
names the run, records a checksum (a fingerprint of a file's contents) of this
file and of every input, records each fit's status and each cache decision
(whether a saved result was reused or computed again), and lists every output
with whether this run wrote it.

**Registration status.** Study 1 is postregistered, meaning its registration
was deposited after the data were collected. The data were collected in 2024,
and the analyses were run before
`Docs/Preregistration/Study1_Preregistration.md` was deposited. That document
says so, and marks which parts of its analysis plan were settled with the
estimates already in view. Nothing in this notebook is a confirmatory test.
The analyses in §2 to §8 are robustness analyses of the kinds the field uses
(Barr et al. 2013; Lakens 2017 for equivalence testing; Kruschke 2018 for the
region of practical equivalence; Simonsohn et al. 2020 for specification
curves).

Two commitments in that document still govern what may be written here. The
first is the confirmatory family: the attribution contrast on creativity, the
attribution contrast on effort, the attribution-by-dimension contrast, and the
H4 variance-ratio test. Those four *p*-values are corrected together in
`Study1_01_Quant.Rmd` by the Holm procedure, a correction that controls the
chance of any false positive across the family, and no test in this file
joins that family. The second concerns the false-discovery-rate columns on the
tables written here. They use the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, which
controls the expected share of false positives among the rows a table calls
positive. The preregistration records those columns as descriptive and as
belonging to a larger set of exploratory quantities, and states that no claim
in the paper rests on them. Each table says the same in its `p_adj_method`
column.

**Reading order.** §2 loads the saved brms fits (`file =`) after brms has
compared each with the current data, formula, priors and Stan code
(`file_refit = "on_change"`). §3 and §4 read the primary lmer fits from
`models/`. §4.1 reads the per-arm variance components from
`tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv`. §5.1, §6 and the length-covariate
specifications in §8 need `nlp/study1_text_measures.csv`.

---

```{r audit-switches}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Switches and registered constants. Each value a reader may want to check
# is set here, with the reason for it, rather than at the point of use.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# §2.2: refit the Gaussian brms models under a wider prior (normal(0, 2.5)
# on b, the fixed-effect coefficients). The refit costs ~10-20 min of Stan
# sampling, so the switch is FALSE by default and the notebook knits from
# the saved fits. Set it to TRUE for the supplement run.
RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY <- FALSE

# §3: the equivalence bounds, in rating points on the five-point scale.
#
# REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND is the bound the preregistration fixes for H3, the
# prediction that the attribution penalty does not differ between figurative
# and non-figurative images. The test at that bound belongs to
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10, beside the model whose term it tests.
# That test is two one-sided tests, each at .05, run under both the
# intercepts-only and the maximal random-effects structures. The number is
# recorded here only so that the sensitivity table below can name the bound
# that carries the verdict and tell it apart from the ones that do not.
REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND <- 0.20

# EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS are the wider bounds the preregistration asks for
# as descriptive sensitivity. They carry no verdict on H3. They answer a
# narrower question: how far the bound would have to be widened before the
# equivalence conclusion changed.
EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS <- c(0.30, 0.50)

# The H1 estimand. Every check in this file that re-estimates H1 reports the
# contrast Study1_01_Quant.Rmd tests: the human-arm mean minus the
# generator-arm mean, averaged with equal weight over the two image kinds.
# H1_TERM is the label that row carries in every table, so a reader looking
# for H1 in any table finds it under one name. The TypeAI coefficient of a
# model with the attribution-by-image-kind interaction is the
# generator-minus-human difference at the non-figurative images only, and its
# rows are labelled that way.
H1_TERM <- "H1 contrast: Human - AI, averaged over image kind"

# The fit statuses whose estimates, intervals and p-values are reported.
# "singular" is among them: a singular fit converged, on the boundary of its
# parameter space, and its fixed effects are usable. "not_converged" and
# "error" are not.
USABLE_STATUS <- c("ok", "singular")

# The saved brms fits in models/ are reused only after brms has compared each
# one with the current data, formula, priors and generated Stan code
# ("on_change"); any difference makes brms refit and save over the file. The
# sampling settings that comparison does not cover (chains, iterations, seed,
# adapt_delta, max_treedepth) are checked against the code in section 2, and
# a saved fit whose settings differ is refitted.
BRMS_FILE_REFIT <- "on_change"

# Multiplicity in this notebook. The preregistration names a confirmatory
# family of four tests: the attribution contrast on creativity, the
# attribution contrast on effort, the attribution-by-dimension contrast, and
# the H4 variance-ratio test. The family is corrected by the Holm procedure,
# in which the tests are ordered from the smallest p-value upward and each is
# compared against a threshold that begins strictest and relaxes as earlier
# tests pass. That correction is applied in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd, and no test
# in this file belongs to that family.
#
# What add_p_adj() attaches to the tables written here is the
# Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment, which controls the
# expected share of false positives among the rows a table calls positive. It
# is computed within dimension, because creativity and effort are separate
# models fitted to separate data. It is descriptive, as the
# preregistration says such columns are, and the p_adj_method column carries
# that label into the deposited file. The intercept is never part of a family,
# and neither is the H1 contrast row: H1 belongs to the confirmatory family
# corrected in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd, and its p_adj_method cell says so. Rows
# whose p is NA stay NA and do not count towards the family size.
add_p_adj <- function(df, p_col = "p.value", within = "dimension",
                      exclude_terms = c("(Intercept)", H1_TERM)) {
  stopifnot(p_col %in% names(df), all(within %in% names(df)))
  has_term <- "term" %in% names(df)
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(within))) %>%
    mutate(
      p_adj = {
        p <- .data[[p_col]]
        if (has_term) p[.data[["term"]] %in% exclude_terms] <- NA_real_
        p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
      },
      p_adj_method = paste0("Benjamini-Hochberg within ",
                            paste(within, collapse = " x "),
                            "; descriptive, not the confirmatory correction")
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(p_adj_method = if (has_term) {
      if_else(.data[["term"]] %in% H1_TERM,
              paste0("not adjusted here: the H1 contrast is corrected with ",
                     "the confirmatory family (Holm) in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd"),
              p_adj_method)
    } else p_adj_method)
}
```

```{r paths}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# As in the other notebooks, every path below is built from PROJECT_ROOT. It
# is the first folder at or above this file's own folder, the working
# directory when the file is knitted, that holds both Data and Analysis; the
# environment variable STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT, when set, names it instead.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROJECT_ROOT <- local({
  is_root <- function(p) dir.exists(file.path(p, "Data")) &&
                         dir.exists(file.path(p, "Analysis"))
  root <- Sys.getenv("STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT")
  if (nzchar(root)) {
    root <- normalizePath(root, mustWork = FALSE)
    if (!is_root(root)) {
      stop("The folder STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT names has no Data and Analysis ",
           "folders.")
    }
  } else {
    root <- normalizePath(getwd(), mustWork = TRUE)
    while (!is_root(root)) {
      if (identical(dirname(root), root)) {
        stop("No folder at or above the working directory holds both Data ",
             "and Analysis. Knit this file from its own folder, or set ",
             "STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT to the project root.")
      }
      root <- dirname(root)
    }
  }
  root
})

STUDY_NUM    <- 1
STUDY_FOLDER <- paste("Study", STUDY_NUM)

PATH_ANALYSIS   <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "Analysis",
                             "R Analysis Pipeline", STUDY_FOLDER)
PATH_OUT        <- PATH_ANALYSIS

PATH_OUT_FIG    <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "figures")
PATH_OUT_MODELS <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "models")
PATH_OUT_NLP    <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "nlp")

PATH_PAPER_TAB  <- file.path(PATH_PAPER, "tables")
PATH_PAPER_FIG  <- file.path(PATH_PAPER, "figures")

if (!dir.exists(PROJECT_ROOT)) {
  stop("PROJECT_ROOT does not exist:\n  ", PROJECT_ROOT)
}

for (p in c(PATH_OUT_TAB, PATH_OUT_FIG, PATH_OUT_MODELS,
            PATH_PAPER_TAB, PATH_PAPER_FIG)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}
```

```{r run-record}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The run record. RUN_LOG collects one row for every input read, model
# fitted, cache decision taken and file written, and section 9 writes it out,
# with the settings and the source checksum, as
# tables/study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv.
#
#   RUN_STARTED_AT  the clock time at which this run began.
#   RUN_ID          that time followed by the first eight characters of a
#                   checksum taken over the checksums of the inputs, the
#                   form Study1_01_Quant.Rmd uses, so two runs on the same
#                   inputs share the suffix and a run on changed inputs does
#                   not.
#
# OUTPUT_FILES lists every file this notebook writes. Each one already on disk
# is deleted here, before anything is computed, so that a section that fails
# or is skipped leaves no table from an earlier run in its place; the
# manifest is among them, so a run that stops part way leaves no manifest.
# write_output() and save_figure() are the only writers: each refuses a path
# that is not on the list and records the file it wrote, with its checksum.
# note_not_written() records why a listed file was not written, for the
# manifest. The brms fits in models/ are not on the list, because they are
# saved fits that section 2 checks before reusing, not results.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RUN_STAGE      <- "robustness"
RUN_STARTED_AT <- Sys.time()

# A SHA-256 checksum is a 64-character fingerprint of a file's contents:
# identical bytes give the same string and any change gives a different one.
# It identifies every input and output in the manifest and keys the knitr
# caches of sections 4 and 8. NA for a file that does not exist.
file_sha256 <- function(path) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(path))
  ok  <- file.exists(path)
  out[ok] <- unname(tools::sha256sum(path[ok]))
  out
}

RUN_INPUT_PATHS <- c(
  file.path(PATH_OUT, "study1_long_with_text.csv"),
  file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, c("study1_lmm_creativity.rds",
                               "study1_lmm_effort.rds")),
  file.path(PATH_OUT_NLP, "study1_text_measures.csv"),
  file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, c("study1_h3_equivalence.csv",
                            "study1_h4_variance_partition.csv",
                            "study1_h4_variance_test.csv",
                            "study1_confirmatory_family.csv"))
)
input_hash_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines(coalesce(file_sha256(RUN_INPUT_PATHS), "absent"), input_hash_file)
RUN_ID <- paste0(format(RUN_STARTED_AT, "%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"), "-",
                 substr(unname(tools::sha256sum(input_hash_file)), 1, 8))
unlink(input_hash_file)

RUN_LOG <- tibble(role = character(), file = character(),
                  item = character(), status = character(),
                  detail = character(), sha256 = character(),
                  recorded_at = character())

# Paths in the manifest are written as Study1_01_Quant.Rmd writes them:
# relative to this Study 1 folder, or under Docs/Writing/Final Paper/ for the
# paper copies, so the manifest reads the same on any machine.
manifest_label <- function(p) {
  vapply(p, function(x) {
    if (startsWith(x, paste0(PATH_OUT, "/"))) {
      substring(x, nchar(PATH_OUT) + 2)
    } else if (startsWith(x, paste0(PATH_PAPER, "/"))) {
      file.path("Docs", "Writing", "Final Paper",
                substring(x, nchar(PATH_PAPER) + 2))
    } else x
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

log_record <- function(role, item, status, detail = "",
                       file = NA_character_, sha256 = NA_character_) {
  RUN_LOG <<- bind_rows(RUN_LOG, tibble(
    role = role, file = file, item = item, status = status,
    detail = detail, sha256 = sha256,
    recorded_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")))
  invisible(NULL)
}

OUTPUT_FILES <- c(
  file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, c(
    "study1_brms_primary_fixed.csv",
    "study1_brms_cumulative_fixed.csv",
    "study1_brms_prior_sensitivity.csv",
    "study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv",
    "study1_sensitivity_power.csv",
    "study1_sensitivity_power_80pct.csv",
    "study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv",
    "study1_h4_resolution.csv",
    "study1_covariate_robustness.csv",
    "study1_length_covariate.csv",
    "study1_engagement_by_condition.csv",
    "study1_engagement_trimmed_fits.csv",
    "study1_engagement_per_participant.csv",
    "study1_stimulus_as_fixed.csv",
    "study1_specification_curve.csv",
    "study1_specification_curve_failures.csv",
    "study1_specification_curve_counts.csv",
    "study1_robustness_h1_contrast.csv",
    "study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv"
  )),
  file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, c(
    "study1_brms_ppc.pdf",
    "study1_specification_curve_creativity.pdf",
    "study1_specification_curve_effort.pdf"
  )),
  file.path(PATH_PAPER_FIG, c(
    "study1_specification_curve_creativity.pdf",
    "study1_specification_curve_effort.pdf"
  ))
)
PATH_MANIFEST <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv")
OUTPUT_NOTES  <- character(0)

outputs_on_disk <- OUTPUT_FILES[file.exists(OUTPUT_FILES)]
if (length(outputs_on_disk) > 0) file.remove(outputs_on_disk)
cat(sprintf("Run %s: %d output files from an earlier run removed before writing.\n",
            RUN_ID, length(outputs_on_disk)))

write_output <- function(df, path) {
  if (!path %in% OUTPUT_FILES) {
    stop("write_output(): ", path, " is not listed in OUTPUT_FILES.")
  }
  write_csv(df, path)
  log_record("output", basename(path), "written",
             sprintf("%d rows x %d columns", nrow(df), ncol(df)),
             file = manifest_label(path), sha256 = file_sha256(path))
}

save_figure <- function(plot, path, ...) {
  if (!path %in% OUTPUT_FILES) {
    stop("save_figure(): ", path, " is not listed in OUTPUT_FILES.")
  }
  ggsave(path, plot, ...)
  log_record("output", basename(path), "written", "figure",
             file = manifest_label(path), sha256 = file_sha256(path))
}

note_not_written <- function(paths, why) {
  OUTPUT_NOTES[paths] <<- why
  invisible(NULL)
}

if (!RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY) {
  note_not_written(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_brms_prior_sensitivity.csv"),
                   "not run: RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY is FALSE")
}

# A knitr-cached chunk (sections 4 and 8) stamps the time it computed its
# results. When knitr restores the chunk from its cache instead of running
# it, the stamp predates this run, and the manifest records the chunk as
# restored, which is only possible when the chunk's code and the checksums of
# its inputs are those of the run that filled the cache.
log_knitr_cache <- function(chunk, computed_at) {
  restored <- computed_at < RUN_STARTED_AT
  log_record("cache", paste("knitr chunk", chunk),
             if (restored) "restored" else "computed",
             if (restored) {
               paste0("results restored from the knitr cache, computed ",
                      format(computed_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                      "; the cache key is the chunk's code and the checksums ",
                      "of its inputs")
             } else "computed in this run")
}
```

```{r load}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load the long-format data and the frequentist LMMs fitted in
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd. The text-measure file supplies response length for
# sections 5.1, 6 and 8.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
long <- read_csv(
  file.path(PATH_OUT, "study1_long_with_text.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    Type          = factor(Type,          levels = c("Human", "AI")),
    stimulus_type = factor(stimulus_type, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure")),
    dimension     = factor(dimension,     levels = c("creativity", "effort")),
    id            = factor(id),
    stimulus_id   = factor(stimulus_id)
  )

creat_res <- readRDS(file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_creativity.rds"))
eff_res   <- readRDS(file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_effort.rds"))

# Every input this notebook may read (RUN_INPUT_PATHS, run-record chunk),
# fingerprinted as it stands at the start of the run. A file that is absent
# is recorded as absent; the sections that need it say what they skip.
for (f in RUN_INPUT_PATHS) {
  log_record("input", basename(f),
             if (file.exists(f)) "read" else "absent",
             file = manifest_label(f), sha256 = file_sha256(f))
}

# Text measures (for sections 5.1, 6 and the length specifications in 8).
# The only column those sections need is n_words, the number of words in the
# justification, which is why the file is read with just its keys and that
# column. It is optional: every section that uses it is gated on the file
# existing, so the notebook still knits from ratings alone.
# id and stimulus_id are converted to factors, as they are in `long`, so
# that the joins below do not fail on a type mismatch.
measures_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_NLP, "study1_text_measures.csv")
nlp <- if (file.exists(measures_path)) {
  read_csv(measures_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::select(id, stimulus_id, dimension, n_words) %>%
    mutate(
      id          = as.factor(as.character(id)),
      stimulus_id = as.factor(as.character(stimulus_id)),
      dimension   = factor(dimension, levels = c("creativity", "effort"))
    )
} else {
  message("Text-measure file not found; the length-based sections will be ",
          "skipped.")
  NULL
}

# The text measures join one row per response. Their keys must be unique and
# must cover exactly the responses in the long file; otherwise a join below
# would silently drop responses or duplicate them.
response_keys <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(long[, response_keys]))
if (!is.null(nlp)) {
  key_chr <- function(df) {
    df %>% dplyr::select(all_of(response_keys)) %>%
      mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(nlp[, response_keys])) {
    stop("nlp/study1_text_measures.csv has more than one row for some ",
         "response. Re-run Study1_02_Text.ipynb.")
  }
  n_missing <- nrow(anti_join(key_chr(long), key_chr(nlp), by = response_keys))
  n_extra   <- nrow(anti_join(key_chr(nlp), key_chr(long), by = response_keys))
  if (n_missing + n_extra > 0) {
    stop("nlp/study1_text_measures.csv does not cover the long data one to ",
         "one: ", n_missing, " responses have no text row and ", n_extra,
         " text rows have no response. Re-run Study1_02_Text.ipynb after ",
         "Study1_01_Quant.Rmd.")
  }
} else {
  note_not_written(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, c(
                     "study1_length_covariate.csv",
                     "study1_engagement_by_condition.csv",
                     "study1_engagement_trimmed_fits.csv",
                     "study1_engagement_per_participant.csv")),
                   "skipped: nlp/study1_text_measures.csv not found")
}

# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd saves each LMM as list(fit = lmerMod, anova = ...,
# ...). unwrap_lmm() takes the fit out of that list, and it also accepts a
# bare lmerMod, so either form gives a usable fit.
unwrap_lmm <- function(obj) {
  if (inherits(obj, c("lmerMod", "lmerModLmerTest"))) return(obj)
  if (!is.null(obj$fit) &&
      inherits(obj$fit, c("lmerMod", "lmerModLmerTest"))) return(obj$fit)
  stop("Could not extract an lmerMod from the saved object. ",
       "Expected either a direct lmerMod or a list with $fit.")
}
creat_fit <- unwrap_lmm(creat_res)
eff_fit   <- unwrap_lmm(eff_res)

# The saved primary fits must have been fitted to the long data read above.
# Each fit's model frame (the rows lme4 used) is compared with that
# dimension's rows of the long file, key by key and rating by rating. A
# difference means Study1_01_Quant.Rmd wrote one file without the other, and
# every comparison below would set a fresh refit beside a stale fit.
check_fit_matches_long <- function(fit, dim_name) {
  mf  <- model.frame(fit)
  dat <- long %>% filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating))
  same <- nrow(mf) == nrow(dat) &&
    identical(as.character(mf$id),          as.character(dat$id)) &&
    identical(as.character(mf$stimulus_id), as.character(dat$stimulus_id)) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(mf$rating), as.numeric(dat$rating)))
  if (!same) {
    stop("models/study1_lmm_", dim_name, ".rds was not fitted to the ",
         dim_name, " rows of study1_long_with_text.csv. Re-run ",
         "Study1_01_Quant.Rmd so the two are written together.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
check_fit_matches_long(creat_fit, "creativity")
check_fit_matches_long(eff_fit,   "effort")

# Convergence records for the lmer fits summarised in sections 5 to 7.
# The knit hides warnings (warning = FALSE in setup-knitr), so a fit that
# lme4 flagged would otherwise leave no trace in the deposited table. This
# helper stamps two columns onto every row of a fit's tidy summary:
#   is_singular       lme4::isSingular(): TRUE when the fit sits on the
#                     boundary of the parameter space, meaning a variance
#                     estimated at zero or, in a model with correlated random
#                     effects, a correlation estimated at plus or minus one.
#                     A singular fit can carry nonzero slope variances (a
#                     correlation at the boundary is enough), so the flag
#                     says the structure is richer than the data support,
#                     not that any particular variance is zero.
#   convergence_note  every message lme4 attached to the fit while checking
#                     its optimum (the gradient, Hessian and optimizer-code
#                     checks, and the boundary note for a singular fit),
#                     plus any warning the optimizer raised, joined with
#                     "; ". "none" means the fit passed every check.
add_lmm_convergence <- function(tab, fit) {
  notes <- c(unlist(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages),
             unlist(fit@optinfo$warnings))
  tab %>%
    mutate(
      is_singular      = lme4::isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-4),
      convergence_note = if (length(notes) == 0) "none" else
                           paste(notes, collapse = "; ")
    )
}
```

```{r h1-helpers}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared by every section below: the status of a fit, the H1 contrast from a
# fit, and the tables that carry both.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- The status of an lmer fit ----------------------------------------------
# "not_converged" when the optimizer returned a nonzero code or lme4 attached
# any message other than the boundary note (a failed gradient, Hessian or
# optimizer check); "singular" when the fit converged on the boundary of the
# parameter space; "ok" otherwise.
lmm_fit_status <- function(fit) {
  msgs <- c(unlist(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages),
            unlist(fit@optinfo$warnings))
  failed_checks <- msgs[!grepl("boundary (singular) fit", msgs, fixed = TRUE)]
  opt_code <- fit@optinfo$conv$opt
  if (length(failed_checks) > 0 || (!is.null(opt_code) && opt_code != 0)) {
    "not_converged"
  } else if (lme4::isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-4)) {
    "singular"
  } else {
    "ok"
  }
}

# ---- A fit that may fail -----------------------------------------------------
# Evaluates the fitting expression and returns list(fit, error): the fit and
# NA, or NULL and the error message, so that one failed model is recorded and
# the run continues.
fit_safely <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch(list(fit = expr, error = NA_character_),
           error = function(e) list(fit = NULL, error = conditionMessage(e)))
}

# ---- What each attribution row of a table estimates --------------------------
estimand_label <- function(term) {
  case_when(
    term == H1_TERM ~
      "H1: Human minus AI, averaged with equal weight over the two image kinds",
    term == "TypeAI" ~
      paste0("AI minus Human at the non-figurative images: a simple effect ",
             "under treatment coding, not the H1 contrast"),
    term == "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure" ~
      paste0("figurative penalty minus non-figurative penalty: the ",
             "attribution x image kind interaction, the H3 quantity"),
    TRUE ~ "not an attribution quantity"
  )
}

# ---- The H1 contrast from a frequentist fit ----------------------------------
# emmeans() builds each arm's estimated marginal mean, averaging the model's
# predictions with equal weight over the two image kinds (and holding any
# covariate at its mean, which leaves an attribution difference unchanged
# because no covariate interacts with attribution), and pairs() takes Human
# minus AI. adjust = "none" keeps emmeans from correcting a single contrast.
# The degrees of freedom are emmeans' own for each model family: for lmer
# that is Kenward-Roger (a small-sample adjustment of the degrees of freedom
# and standard error for mixed models), the method of the H1 test in
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd. df_override fixes them where the model family sets the
# reference distribution (Inf, the normal distribution, for the ordinal and
# GEE fits; G - 1 for the participant-level fits with cluster-robust standard
# errors), and vcov_override passes a covariance matrix other than the
# model's own. The estimate is checked against the same linear combination
# written out from the coefficients, minus TypeAI minus half the interaction
# (minus TypeAI alone in a model without the interaction), so the emmeans
# reading and the coefficients cannot disagree unnoticed.
h1_contrast_freq <- function(fit, data, df_override = NULL,
                             vcov_override = NULL) {
  args <- list(fit, specs = ~ Type, data = data)
  if (!is.null(vcov_override)) args$vcov. <- vcov_override
  emm <- suppressMessages(do.call(emmeans::emmeans, args))
  con <- pairs(emm, adjust = "none")
  if (!is.null(df_override)) con <- update(con, df = df_override)
  s <- as.data.frame(summary(con, infer = TRUE))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1, s$contrast == "Human - AI")
  b   <- if (inherits(fit, "merMod")) lme4::fixef(fit) else coef(fit)
  int <- "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"
  by_hand <- -(b[["TypeAI"]] + if (int %in% names(b)) 0.5 * b[[int]] else 0)
  if (abs(s$estimate - by_hand) > 1e-6) {
    stop("h1_contrast_freq(): emmeans gives ", signif(s$estimate, 8),
         " and the coefficients give ", signif(by_hand, 8), ".")
  }
  lo <- intersect(c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"), names(s))
  hi <- intersect(c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"), names(s))
  st <- intersect(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio"), names(s))
  tibble(estimate = s$estimate, se = s$SE, df = s$df,
         ci_lo = s[[lo]], ci_hi = s[[hi]], statistic = s[[st]],
         p = s$p.value)
}

# ---- The H1 contrast from a brms fit -----------------------------------------
# The same emmeans call on a brmsfit returns the contrast once per posterior
# draw, so the contrast has a full posterior, summarised in the columns the
# brms tables use: mean, median, the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (the 95 per
# cent credible interval, the range holding 95 per cent of the posterior),
# the probability of direction, and the sampler diagnostics of the contrast's
# own draws, computed chain by chain. For a cumulative model emmeans works on
# the latent scale and leaves out the thresholds (the cut points between
# adjacent rating categories), which cancel in a difference between arms; the
# warning brms raises about that is muffled here for that reason. The draws
# are checked against minus b_TypeAI minus half the interaction, draw by draw.
h1_contrast_brms <- function(fit) {
  emm <- withCallingHandlers(
    emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ Type),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("ordinal models is experimental", conditionMessage(w))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    })
  con <- pairs(emm)
  by_chain <- coda::as.mcmc(con, sep.chains = TRUE)
  dr <- posterior::as_draws_df(by_chain)
  v  <- as.numeric(dr[[posterior::variables(dr)[1]]])
  pd_all  <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit)
  by_hand <- -(pd_all$b_TypeAI + 0.5 * pd_all[["b_TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"]])
  if (length(v) != length(by_hand) ||
      max(abs(sort(v) - sort(by_hand))) > 1e-8) {
    stop("h1_contrast_brms(): the emmeans draws differ from the coefficient ",
         "draws.")
  }
  dg <- posterior::summarise_draws(dr, "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  tibble(mean = mean(v), median = median(v),
         ci_lo = quantile(v, 0.025, names = FALSE),
         ci_hi = quantile(v, 0.975, names = FALSE),
         pd = max(mean(v > 0), mean(v < 0)),
         rhat = dg$rhat, ess_bulk = dg$ess_bulk, ess_tail = dg$ess_tail)
}

# ---- An lmer fit's table, with the H1 row ------------------------------------
# The fixed-effect table of one lmer fit, the H1 contrast appended as its own
# row (effect "estimated marginal contrast"), each attribution row's estimand
# named, the scale named, and the fit's status on every row. The H1 row's
# interval is emmeans' t interval on Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom; the
# coefficient rows keep the t interval on Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
# that broom.mixed reports for an lmerTest fit. (For the H1 contrast of the
# two primary fits the two methods give the same 109 degrees of freedom and
# the same standard error.) A fit that errored gives one row saying so.
# A fit that did not converge keeps its estimates and standard errors for
# inspection, and its test statistics, p-values and intervals are set to NA,
# so that no reading can be taken from it.
# The one row a table carries for a fit that errored: every column of a
# fitted table, NA, with the error message as the convergence note.
error_row <- function(dim_name, estimand, message) {
  tibble(dimension = dim_name, effect = NA_character_, term = H1_TERM,
         estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_, statistic = NA_real_,
         df = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_, conf.low = NA_real_,
         conf.high = NA_real_, estimand = estimand, scale = "rating points",
         is_singular = NA, convergence_note = message, fit_status = "error")
}

tidy_with_h1 <- function(res, dim_name, label, data) {
  if (is.null(res$fit)) {
    log_record("fit", label, "error", res$error)
    return(error_row(dim_name, estimand_label(H1_TERM), res$error))
  }
  fit    <- res$fit
  status <- lmm_fit_status(fit)
  h1     <- h1_contrast_freq(fit, data)
  tab <- broom.mixed::tidy(fit, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(effect = "estimated marginal contrast", term = H1_TERM,
                     estimate = h1$estimate, std.error = h1$se,
                     statistic = h1$statistic, df = h1$df, p.value = h1$p,
                     conf.low = h1$ci_lo, conf.high = h1$ci_hi)) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim_name,
           estimand  = estimand_label(term),
           scale     = "rating points") %>%
    add_lmm_convergence(fit) %>%
    mutate(fit_status = status)
  if (!status %in% USABLE_STATUS) {
    tab <- tab %>%
      mutate(across(c(statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high), ~ NA_real_))
  }
  log_record("fit", label, status, tab$convergence_note[1])
  tab
}

# ---- The H1 contrast across the checks --------------------------------------
# Each section adds its H1 rows here, beside the TypeAI simple effect the same
# model gives; section 8.2 writes the collection as
# tables/study1_robustness_h1_contrast.csv.
H1_SUMMARY <- tibble()
add_h1_summary <- function(check, section, dimension, model, scale,
                           estimate, se, df, interval, ci_lo, ci_hi, p,
                           pd = NA_real_, contrast_method,
                           typeai_estimate, typeai_ci_lo, typeai_ci_hi,
                           fit_status) {
  H1_SUMMARY <<- bind_rows(H1_SUMMARY, tibble(
    check, section, dimension, model, scale,
    estimand = estimand_label(H1_TERM),
    estimate, se, df, interval, ci_lo, ci_hi, p, pd, contrast_method,
    typeai_simple_effect = typeai_estimate,
    typeai_ci_lo, typeai_ci_hi, fit_status))
  invisible(NULL)
}

# The H1 rows of an lmer table, passed to add_h1_summary().
summarise_lmm_table <- function(tab, check, section, model) {
  for (dm in unique(tab$dimension)) {
    t1 <- tab %>% filter(dimension == dm)
    h  <- t1 %>% filter(term == H1_TERM)
    ty <- t1 %>% filter(term == "TypeAI")
    add_h1_summary(
      check = check, section = section, dimension = dm, model = model,
      scale = "rating points",
      estimate = h$estimate %||% NA_real_, se = h$std.error %||% NA_real_,
      df = h$df %||% NA_real_,
      interval = "95% confidence interval (t, Kenward-Roger df)",
      ci_lo = h$conf.low %||% NA_real_, ci_hi = h$conf.high %||% NA_real_,
      p = h$p.value %||% NA_real_,
      contrast_method = "emmeans on the Type x image kind model, Human - AI averaged over image kind",
      typeai_estimate = if (nrow(ty)) ty$estimate else NA_real_,
      typeai_ci_lo    = if (nrow(ty)) ty$conf.low else NA_real_,
      typeai_ci_hi    = if (nrow(ty)) ty$conf.high else NA_real_,
      fit_status = h$fit_status)
  }
}

# The primary fits of Study1_01_Quant.Rmd, the reference every other row is a
# variation on. Their H1 contrast is checked against the one that file
# deposited in its confirmatory family, when that table is on disk.
primary_tables <- bind_rows(
  tidy_with_h1(list(fit = creat_fit), "creativity",
               "primary LMM (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd), creativity",
               long %>% filter(dimension == "creativity")),
  tidy_with_h1(list(fit = eff_fit), "effort",
               "primary LMM (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd), effort",
               long %>% filter(dimension == "effort"))
)
summarise_lmm_table(primary_tables, "primary model (reference)",
                    "Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7",
                    "rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)")
conf_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_confirmatory_family.csv")
if (file.exists(conf_path)) {
  conf_h1 <- read_csv(conf_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(hypothesis == "H1")
  ref <- H1_SUMMARY %>% filter(check == "primary model (reference)")
  for (dm in ref$dimension) {
    dep <- conf_h1$estimate[grepl(dm, conf_h1$test)]
    here <- ref$estimate[ref$dimension == dm]
    agree <- length(dep) == 1 && abs(dep - here) < 1e-6
    log_record("input", paste("H1 contrast,", dm,
                              "(confirmatory family against the model file)"),
               if (agree) "agrees" else "differs",
               sprintf("study1_confirmatory_family.csv %s; recomputed %.6f",
                       paste(signif(dep, 7), collapse = ", "), here))
    if (!agree) {
      warning("The H1 contrast recomputed from models/study1_lmm_", dm,
              ".rds differs from tables/study1_confirmatory_family.csv.")
    }
  }
}
print(as.data.frame(H1_SUMMARY %>%
  dplyr::select(dimension, estimate, se, df, ci_lo, ci_hi, p,
                typeai_simple_effect)))
```

# 2. Bayesian replication of primary LMMs (brms)

```{r brms-primary}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The frequentist LMMs (section 7 of 01_Quant) treat the 1-5 Likert
# response as continuous. They are fitted by REML (restricted maximum
# likelihood, which estimates the variance components after removing the
# part of the data the fixed effects explain) and tested with Satterthwaite
# df (degrees of freedom approximated from the estimated variances rather
# than fixed by the sample size). Here both dimensions are refitted in brms
# with the same fixed effects, crossed random intercepts (a baseline for
# each participant and for each image), a Gaussian likelihood and weakly
# informative priors.
#
# What this section shows, and what it does not. The brms CrIs (credible
# intervals: the Bayesian interval holding 95% of the posterior) may agree
# with the lmer CIs. That agreement does not show that treating the Likert
# response as continuous is defensible, because this model uses the SAME
# Gaussian likelihood as the LMM. With weak priors and N = 2,220 the
# posterior is bound to track the MLE, the maximum-likelihood estimate (the
# Bernstein-von Mises result: with enough data the posterior concentrates
# on the likelihood's estimate whatever weak prior was used). Agreement
# therefore says only that the reported effects are not artefacts of (i)
# the REML and Satterthwaite small-sample adjustments or (ii) the choice of
# prior.
# Whether a Gaussian likelihood suits a bounded 1-5 ordinal response is a
# DIFFERENT question. The cumulative-ordinal fit in §2.1 answers it
# (agreement in sign and size on the latent scale, the continuous scale the
# ordinal model assumes beneath the five categories), and so do the PPC
# figures (posterior predictive checks: ratings simulated from the fitted
# model, drawn over the observed distribution). The manuscript must not cite
# §2 as evidence for the likelihood.
#
# Prior choices:
#   Intercept          student_t(3, 0, 2.5)   - brms default; weakly informative
#   Fixed coefs (b)    normal(0, 1)           - 95% mass within -2 to +2 rating
#                                                units (realistic for Likert)
#   Random-effect SDs  student_t(3, 0, 2.5)
#   Residual sigma     student_t(3, 0, 2.5)
#
# How weak is normal(0, 1) on b here? The observed TypeAI coefficients
# (the simple effects at the non-figurative images) are ~ -0.41 (creativity)
# and ~ -0.91 (effort) rating points with SEs ~0.14, and the H1 contrasts are
# 0.45 and 0.92 with SEs 0.13 and 0.15, so the argument below holds for both.
# A normal(0, 1) prior has density ratio p(0)/p(0.91) = exp(0.91^2/2) ~ 1.5:
# it favours zero over the observed effort effect by a factor of only ~1.5,
# and the likelihood is ~40x more concentrated than the prior (SE 0.14 vs
# SD 1). The prior therefore shrinks the posterior mean by at most ~2% of
# the estimate, which makes it only WEAKLY informative for effects of
# 0.4-0.9. §2.2 checks this by refitting with normal(0, 2.5), behind the
# switch RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY.
#
# SAVED FITS. Each fit is saved to models/ through `file =`, and a later run
# reuses it only under the policy set in the switches chunk
# (BRMS_FILE_REFIT, "on_change"): brms compares the saved fit with the
# current data, formula, priors and generated Stan code, and refits on any
# difference. fit_brms_cached() adds the check brms does not make, on the
# sampling settings stored in the saved fit (chains, iterations, seed,
# adapt_delta, max_treedepth); a saved fit whose settings differ from the
# ones below is refitted. Each decision (reused, refitted, or fitted because
# no saved fit existed) goes to the run record with the file's checksum. The
# chunk carries no knitr cache, so that the brms check runs on every knit
# rather than being skipped with the chunk.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fit_brms_cached <- function(label, file_stub, formula, data, family, prior,
                            chains = 4, iter = 4000, seed = 20260421,
                            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)) {
  rds        <- paste0(file_stub, ".rds")
  had_file   <- file.exists(rds)
  sha_before <- file_sha256(rds)
  refit_mode <- BRMS_FILE_REFIT
  settings_note <- ""
  if (had_file) {
    saved <- readRDS(rds)
    sa    <- saved$fit@stan_args[[1]]
    # Stan's defaults apply where a control value was not set: adapt_delta
    # 0.8 and max_treedepth 10.
    stored <- c(chains        = saved$fit@sim$chains,
                iter          = saved$fit@sim$iter,
                seed          = as.numeric(sa$seed),
                adapt_delta   = sa$control$adapt_delta   %||% 0.8,
                max_treedepth = sa$control$max_treedepth %||% 10)
    wanted <- c(chains        = chains,
                iter          = iter,
                seed          = seed,
                adapt_delta   = control$adapt_delta   %||% 0.8,
                max_treedepth = control$max_treedepth %||% 10)
    if (!isTRUE(all.equal(stored, wanted))) {
      refit_mode <- "always"
      settings_note <- paste0(
        "the sampling settings stored in the saved fit (",
        paste(names(stored), stored, sep = " = ", collapse = ", "),
        ") differ from the code (",
        paste(names(wanted), wanted, sep = " = ", collapse = ", "), ")")
    }
    rm(saved)
  }
  fit <- brm(formula, data = data, family = family, prior = prior,
             chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = 4, seed = seed,
             control = control, file = file_stub, file_refit = refit_mode)
  sha_after <- file_sha256(rds)
  decision <- if (!had_file) "fitted"
              else if (refit_mode == "always" ||
                       !identical(sha_before, sha_after)) "refitted"
              else "reused"
  detail <- switch(decision,
    fitted   = "no saved fit on disk; fitted and saved",
    reused   = paste0("saved fit reused: brms compared it with the current ",
                      "data, formula, priors and Stan code and found no ",
                      "difference, and its sampling settings match the code"),
    refitted = if (nzchar(settings_note)) {
                 paste0("refitted because ", settings_note)
               } else {
                 paste0("refitted: brms found a difference in the data, ",
                        "formula, priors or Stan code and saved the new fit ",
                        "over the old file")
               })
  log_record("cache", label, decision,
             detail, file = manifest_label(rds), sha256 = sha_after)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %s\n", label, decision))
  fit
}

fit_bayesian_primary <- function(dim_name, data = long) {

  dat <- data %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(
      Type          = factor(Type,          levels = c("Human", "AI")),
      stimulus_type = factor(stimulus_type, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure"))
    )

  pri <- c(
    prior(normal(0, 1),        class = b),
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = Intercept),
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = sd),
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = sigma)
  )

  fit_brms_cached(
    label     = paste("brms primary (Gaussian),", dim_name),
    file_stub = file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS,
                          paste0("study1_brms_primary_", dim_name)),
    formula   = rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data      = dat,
    family    = gaussian(),
    prior     = pri,
    chains    = 4,
    iter      = 4000,
    seed      = 20260421,
    control   = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
  )
}

bayes_creat <- fit_bayesian_primary("creativity")
bayes_eff   <- fit_bayesian_primary("effort")
```

```{r brms-primary-summaries}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Bayesian posteriors, summarised for comparison with the frequentist
# fixed effects. For each coefficient the table reports:
#   - Posterior mean and 95% CrI
#   - Probability of direction (Pd): P(sign matches posterior mean)
#   - Rhat, bulk ESS, tail ESS (per coefficient), the max Rhat over ALL
#     parameters (incl. random effects), and the number of divergent
#     transitions, as convergence diagnostics.
#
# ess_tail (effective sample size, the number of independent draws the
# correlated sampler draws are worth, computed in the posterior's tails),
# rhat_max_all_params (the largest Rhat, the between-chain to within-chain
# variance ratio, over every parameter), ess_bulk_min_all_params and
# ess_tail_min_all_params (the smallest effective sample sizes over every
# parameter, random effects and variances included), n_divergent (the count
# of divergent transitions, sampler steps where the numerical integrator
# broke down) and n_max_treedepth (the number of iterations that reached the
# sampler's maximum tree depth, max_treedepth) are written to the CSV rather
# than printed only to the console.
#
# The convergence gate, brms_fit_diagnostics(). A fit is "ok" when every
# reported row (each fixed effect and the H1 contrast) has Rhat < 1.01 and
# bulk and tail ESS > 400 (Vehtari et al. 2021; 400 is 100 per chain over 4
# chains), when the same holds for the largest Rhat and the smallest ESS over
# every parameter of the model, and when no transition diverged. Otherwise
# the fit is "not_converged", the fit_status column of every row of that fit
# says so with the reason, and the run record carries it; the remedy is to
# refit with a longer run, not to read the table. Iterations that reached
# the maximum tree depth are counted and reported but do not fail the gate:
# in Stan's guidance that is a warning about sampling efficiency, not a sign
# that the draws are biased.
# In brms 2.23.0, summary(fit)$fixed has the columns
#   Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
# and nuts_params(fit) is long-format (Chain, Iteration, Parameter, Value)
# with Parameter a factor containing "divergent__" and "treedepth__".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

brms_fit_diagnostics <- function(fit) {
  np <- brms::nuts_params(fit)
  stopifnot(all(c("Parameter", "Value") %in% names(np)))
  par <- as.character(np$Parameter)
  td_limit <- fit$fit@stan_args[[1]]$control$max_treedepth %||% 10
  all_params <- posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_df(fit),
                                           "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  list(
    rhat_max_all_params     = max(all_params$rhat,     na.rm = TRUE),
    ess_bulk_min_all_params = min(all_params$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
    ess_tail_min_all_params = min(all_params$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_divergent             = sum(np$Value[par == "divergent__"]),
    n_max_treedepth         = sum(np$Value[par == "treedepth__"] >= td_limit),
    max_treedepth           = td_limit
  )
}

summarize_brms_fixed <- function(fit, dim_name, label,
                                 scale = "rating points") {
  post <- as_draws_df(fit)
  fixed_cols <- grep("^b_", names(post), value = TRUE)
  sf <- summary(fit)$fixed
  stopifnot(all(c("Rhat", "Bulk_ESS", "Tail_ESS") %in% colnames(sf)))
  dg <- brms_fit_diagnostics(fit)
  fixed_rows <- map_dfr(fixed_cols, function(col) {
    d  <- post[[col]]
    tm <- sub("^b_", "", col)
    tibble(
      dimension = dim_name,
      term      = tm,
      mean      = mean(d),
      median    = median(d),
      ci_lo     = quantile(d, 0.025),
      ci_hi     = quantile(d, 0.975),
      pd        = max(mean(d > 0), mean(d < 0)),
      rhat      = sf[tm, "Rhat"],
      ess_bulk  = sf[tm, "Bulk_ESS"],
      ess_tail  = sf[tm, "Tail_ESS"]
    )
  })
  h1_row <- h1_contrast_brms(fit) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim_name, term = H1_TERM)
  tab <- bind_rows(fixed_rows, h1_row) %>%
    mutate(estimand = estimand_label(term), scale = scale,
           !!!dg)
  failed <- c(
    if (any(tab$rhat >= 1.01))  "a reported row has Rhat >= 1.01",
    if (any(tab$ess_bulk <= 400) || any(tab$ess_tail <= 400))
      "a reported row has bulk or tail ESS <= 400",
    if (dg$rhat_max_all_params >= 1.01)
      "the largest Rhat over all parameters is >= 1.01",
    if (dg$ess_bulk_min_all_params <= 400 || dg$ess_tail_min_all_params <= 400)
      "the smallest ESS over all parameters is <= 400",
    if (dg$n_divergent > 0) "divergent transitions occurred")
  status <- if (length(failed) == 0) "ok" else "not_converged"
  detail <- sprintf(paste0(
    "max Rhat (all parameters) %.4f; min bulk ESS %.0f; min tail ESS %.0f; ",
    "%d divergent transitions; %d iterations at max_treedepth %d%s"),
    dg$rhat_max_all_params, dg$ess_bulk_min_all_params,
    dg$ess_tail_min_all_params, dg$n_divergent, dg$n_max_treedepth,
    dg$max_treedepth,
    if (length(failed)) paste0("; failed: ", paste(failed, collapse = "; "))
    else "")
  log_record("fit", label, status, detail)
  cat(sprintf("%s: convergence %s (%s)\n", label, status, detail))
  if (status != "ok") {
    warning(label, " did not pass the convergence gate: ",
            paste(failed, collapse = "; "))
  }
  tab %>% mutate(fit_status = status)
}

brms_primary_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarize_brms_fixed(bayes_creat, "creativity",
                       "brms primary (Gaussian), creativity"),
  summarize_brms_fixed(bayes_eff,   "effort",
                       "brms primary (Gaussian), effort")
)
brms_primary_summary

# The status of each Gaussian fit, read by section 3's region of practical
# equivalence.
brms_status <- brms_primary_summary %>%
  distinct(dimension, fit_status) %>%
  { setNames(.$fit_status, .$dimension) }

write_output(brms_primary_summary,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_brms_primary_fixed.csv"))

# The H1 rows for section 8.2, beside the TypeAI simple effect of the same
# fit. The interval is the 95 per cent credible interval, so p is NA and the
# probability of direction is reported in its place. A fit that failed the
# convergence gate gives NA for the interval.
add_brms_h1_summary <- function(tab, check, section, model, scale) {
  for (dm in unique(tab$dimension)) {
    h  <- tab %>% filter(dimension == dm, term == H1_TERM)
    ty <- tab %>% filter(dimension == dm, term == "TypeAI")
    ok <- h$fit_status %in% USABLE_STATUS
    add_h1_summary(
      check = check, section = section,
      dimension = sub("_cumulative$", "", dm), model = model, scale = scale,
      estimate = h$mean, se = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
      interval = "95% credible interval (2.5th to 97.5th posterior percentiles)",
      ci_lo = if (ok) h$ci_lo else NA_real_,
      ci_hi = if (ok) h$ci_hi else NA_real_,
      p = NA_real_, pd = if (ok) h$pd else NA_real_,
      contrast_method = "emmeans on the brms posterior draws, Human - AI averaged over image kind",
      typeai_estimate = ty$mean, typeai_ci_lo = ty$ci_lo, typeai_ci_hi = ty$ci_hi,
      fit_status = h$fit_status)
  }
}
add_brms_h1_summary(brms_primary_summary, "Bayesian replication, Gaussian",
                    "section 2",
                    "brms: rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), gaussian",
                    "rating points")

# Posterior predictive checks, saved as one figure for the supplement.
pp_creat <- pp_check(bayes_creat, ndraws = 100) +
  ggtitle("Posterior predictive check: Creativity")
pp_eff <- pp_check(bayes_eff, ndraws = 100) +
  ggtitle("Posterior predictive check: Effort")
pp_combined <- pp_creat / pp_eff
save_figure(pp_combined, file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_brms_ppc.pdf"),
            width = 7, height = 7, device = cairo_pdf)
pp_combined
```

## 2.1 Cumulative-ordinal Bayesian version

```{r brms-cumulative}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# If the Gaussian PPC above shows problems (for example, ratings piled at
# the floor or ceiling of the 1-5 scale in a way the Gaussian does not
# reproduce), the cumulative-ordinal version is the model to use: a
# Bayesian mixed model that treats the five ratings as ordered categories.
# The model is fitted either way, as a supplement, and the paper can lead
# with whichever model has the cleaner PPC. Its coefficients and its H1
# contrast are on the log-odds scale of the cumulative logit model, not in
# rating points. The saved fits are reused under the same policy as
# section 2.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fit_bayesian_cumulative <- function(dim_name) {
  dat <- long %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(
      rating_ord    = factor(rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE),
      Type          = factor(Type,          levels = c("Human", "AI")),
      stimulus_type = factor(stimulus_type, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure"))
    )

  fit_brms_cached(
    label     = paste("brms cumulative (ordinal),", dim_name),
    file_stub = file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS,
                          paste0("study1_brms_cumulative_", dim_name)),
    formula   = rating_ord ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data      = dat,
    family    = cumulative("logit"),
    prior     = c(prior(normal(0, 1), class = b),
                  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = Intercept),
                  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = sd)),
    chains    = 4,
    iter      = 4000,
    seed      = 20260421,
    control   = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)
  )
}

bayes_cum_creat <- fit_bayesian_cumulative("creativity")
bayes_cum_eff   <- fit_bayesian_cumulative("effort")

# Same convergence gate as §2 (see brms_fit_diagnostics for the thresholds).
brms_cum_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarize_brms_fixed(bayes_cum_creat, "creativity_cumulative",
                       "brms cumulative (ordinal), creativity",
                       scale = "log-odds (cumulative logit)"),
  summarize_brms_fixed(bayes_cum_eff,   "effort_cumulative",
                       "brms cumulative (ordinal), effort",
                       scale = "log-odds (cumulative logit)")
)
write_output(brms_cum_summary,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_brms_cumulative_fixed.csv"))
add_brms_h1_summary(brms_cum_summary,
                    "Bayesian replication, cumulative ordinal", "section 2.1",
                    "brms: rating_ord ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), cumulative logit",
                    "log-odds (cumulative logit)")
brms_cum_summary
```

## 2.2 Prior sensitivity (gated; default OFF)

```{r brms-prior-sensitivity}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prior-sensitivity refit of the Gaussian primary models with a wider prior
# on the fixed effects.
#
# Why: the §2 prior normal(0, 1) on b is only WEAKLY informative for effects
# of ~0.4-0.9 rating points (see the §2 header: prior density ratio
# p(0)/p(0.91) ~ 1.5 against a likelihood ~40x tighter). The refit asks
# whether a flatter prior would still move the CrI. normal(0, 2.5) puts 95%
# prior mass on [-5, +5], which covers every difference the 1-5 scale
# allows, so it is essentially uninformative for a Likert contrast. If the
# posterior means and CrIs move by less than, say, 5% of the SE, the choice
# of prior is settled.
#
# Gated by RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY (default FALSE in the `audit-switches`
# chunk) because it adds ~10-20 min of Stan sampling. The gate is an if()
# inside the chunk rather than a chunk option, so that a purled copy of this
# notebook (its code extracted to a plain R script by knitr::purl()) carries
# the same gate. Saved to
# models/study1_brms_primary_<dim>_priorwide.rds once run and reused under
# the policy of section 2, so the gate only needs to be TRUE the first time.
# The H1 contrast is among the rows compared across the two priors.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY) {

fit_bayesian_primary_wideprior <- function(dim_name, data = long) {
  dat <- data %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(
      Type          = factor(Type,          levels = c("Human", "AI")),
      stimulus_type = factor(stimulus_type, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure"))
    )
  pri <- c(
    prior(normal(0, 2.5),       class = b),          # <- the only change vs §2
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = Intercept),
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = sd),
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = sigma)
  )
  fit_brms_cached(
    label     = paste("brms primary (Gaussian, wide prior),", dim_name),
    file_stub = file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS,
                          paste0("study1_brms_primary_", dim_name, "_priorwide")),
    formula   = rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data      = dat,
    family    = gaussian(),
    prior     = pri,
    chains    = 4,
    iter      = 4000,
    seed      = 20260421,
    control   = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
  )
}

bayes_creat_wide <- fit_bayesian_primary_wideprior("creativity")
bayes_eff_wide   <- fit_bayesian_primary_wideprior("effort")

brms_prior_sens <- bind_rows(
  brms_primary_summary %>% mutate(prior_b = "normal(0, 1)"),
  bind_rows(
    summarize_brms_fixed(bayes_creat_wide, "creativity",
                         "brms primary (Gaussian, wide prior), creativity"),
    summarize_brms_fixed(bayes_eff_wide,   "effort",
                         "brms primary (Gaussian, wide prior), effort")
  ) %>% mutate(prior_b = "normal(0, 2.5)")
) %>%
  relocate(prior_b, .after = dimension) %>%
  group_by(dimension, term) %>%
  mutate(
    # shift of the posterior mean between priors, as a fraction of the
    # posterior SD under the default prior: the quantity that says whether
    # the prior matters.
    mean_shift_vs_default   = mean - mean[prior_b == "normal(0, 1)"],
    posterior_sd_default    = (ci_hi[prior_b == "normal(0, 1)"] -
                               ci_lo[prior_b == "normal(0, 1)"]) / (2 * 1.96),
    mean_shift_in_sd_units  = mean_shift_vs_default / posterior_sd_default
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

brms_prior_sens
write_output(brms_prior_sens,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_brms_prior_sensitivity.csv"))

} else {
  cat("Prior sensitivity not run: RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY is FALSE.\n")
}
```

---

# 3. Equivalence sensitivity for H3 at the wider bounds

H3 predicts that the attribution penalty does not differ between figurative and
non-figurative images. It is a prediction of no effect, so a non-significant
interaction term is not by itself evidence for it: failing to detect an effect
is not evidence that there is none. The test that can support it is an
equivalence test. Its form here is two one-sided tests: the estimate is tested
against each end of a stated bound separately, each at .05, and equivalence is
concluded only if both tests reject.

**The registered test is not run here.** It is run in `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd`
section 7.10, at the registered bound of ±0.20 rating points and under both the
intercepts-only and the maximal random-effects structures, beside the model
whose interaction term it tests. That is where the verdict on H3 is decided,
against the four-cell table in the preregistration.

This section runs the descriptive sensitivity the preregistration asks for
alongside that test, at the wider bounds of 0.30 and 0.50 rating points, in two
forms: the frequentist two one-sided tests on the interaction coefficient of
each primary model, and the Bayesian counterpart, in which the bound is treated
as a region of practical equivalence and the question is how much of the
posterior falls inside it. Neither carries a verdict. What they say is how far
the bound would have to be widened before the equivalence conclusion changed.

```{r equivalence-sensitivity, warning=TRUE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two helpers, one frequentist and one Bayesian, each documented with the
# contract it expects, followed by the sensitivity grid they are run over.
#
# BOUNDS. Every bound below is in rating points on the five-point scale, the
# same units as the coefficient being tested, so a bound of 0.30 means "a
# difference between the figurative and non-figurative penalties smaller than
# three tenths of a scale point". The registered bound is 0.20 and is tested
# elsewhere; the bounds run here are wider, and wider bounds make equivalence
# easier to conclude, which is why nothing here is allowed to count as support.
#
# DECISION RULES, stated so the columns can be read without the code.
#   Two one-sided tests: the interval that matters is the 90 per cent one
#     (1 - 2 x alpha, with alpha = .05 on each side). The estimate is inside
#     the bound when that whole interval lies inside it, which happens exactly
#     when the larger of the two one-sided p-values falls below alpha.
#   Region of practical equivalence: Kruschke's (2018) rule on the 95 per cent
#     highest-density interval, the narrowest interval containing 95 per cent
#     of the posterior. The estimate is inside the bound when that interval
#     lies entirely inside it, outside when it lies entirely outside, and
#     neither when it straddles an edge. The share of the whole posterior
#     inside the bound is reported beside it, because it is the more graded
#     answer and does not turn on where one interval happens to end.
#
# No multiplicity column is attached to this table. Its rows are one term
# tested against a series of nested bounds, not a family of hypotheses: the
# p-value is a monotone function of the bound, so adjusting across the rows
# would be adjusting a quantity against itself.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- Helper 1: two one-sided tests on one term of a (g)lmer fit -------------
# INPUT CONTRACT
#   fit   : lmerModLmerTest (Satterthwaite degrees of freedom available, so
#           the tests are t-based) or glmerMod (no degrees of freedom, so the
#           tests are Wald z with df = Inf). A bare lmerMod fitted without
#           lmerTest carries no df column and is REJECTED rather than tested
#           with naive degrees of freedom.
#   term  : exact row name in summary(fit)$coefficients, e.g.
#           "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure".
#   bound : symmetric half-width on the model's linear-predictor scale
#           (rating points for these fits).
#   alpha : one-sided alpha for each of the two tests (default .05, which
#           makes the reported interval a 90 per cent one).
# OUTPUT: one-row tibble whose columns are shared with rope_on_brms_term(),
#         so the two can be bind_rows()-ed into one table.
tost_on_lmer_term <- function(fit, term, bound, alpha = 0.05) {
  stopifnot(inherits(fit, "merMod"),
            is.character(term), length(term) == 1,
            is.numeric(bound), length(bound) == 1, is.finite(bound), bound > 0)
  co <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
  if (!term %in% rownames(co)) {
    stop("tost_on_lmer_term(): term '", term, "' not in fit. Available: ",
         paste(rownames(co), collapse = ", "))
  }
  is_z <- "z value" %in% colnames(co)
  if (!is_z && !"df" %in% colnames(co)) {
    stop("tost_on_lmer_term(): fit has neither Satterthwaite df nor z ",
         "values. Refit with lmerTest::lmer() (linear) or pass a glmerMod.")
  }
  est <- co[term, "Estimate"]
  se  <- co[term, "Std. Error"]
  df  <- if (is_z) Inf else co[term, "df"]
  if (anyNA(c(est, se, df))) {
    stop("tost_on_lmer_term(): NA estimate/SE/df for '", term, "'.")
  }
  # First test: the coefficient is at or below the lower bound. Rejecting it
  # needs a large positive t. Second test: the coefficient is at or above the
  # upper bound, and rejecting that needs a large negative t.
  t_low  <- (est + bound) / se
  t_high <- (est - bound) / se
  p_low  <- pt(t_low,  df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_high <- pt(t_high, df, lower.tail = TRUE)
  crit   <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  tost_p <- max(p_low, p_high)
  tibble(
    method     = if (is_z) "two one-sided tests (Wald z on model term)"
                 else "two one-sided tests (Satterthwaite t on model term)",
    term       = term,
    scale      = if (is_z) "linear predictor (log-odds)"
                 else "linear predictor (rating points)",
    bound_lo   = -bound,
    bound_hi   =  bound,
    estimate   = est,
    se         = se,
    df         = df,
    ci90_lo    = est - crit * se,
    ci90_hi    = est + crit * se,
    tost_p_low = p_low,
    tost_p_high = p_high,
    tost_p     = tost_p,
    nhst_p     = if (is_z) co[term, "Pr(>|z|)"] else co[term, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    reading    = if (tost_p < alpha) "the 90% interval lies inside this bound"
                 else "the 90% interval crosses this bound"
  )
}

# ---- Helper 2: region of practical equivalence on one term of a brmsfit ----
# INPUT CONTRACT
#   fit   : brmsfit (any family). The term is read from the posterior draws,
#           so it must be the exact draw column name, which for a fixed
#           effect carries a leading "b_", e.g. "b_TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure".
#   bound : symmetric half-width on the linear-predictor scale, in the same
#           units as the coefficient.
#   ci    : the mass of the highest-density interval used for the decision
#           rule (default 0.95).
# OUTPUT: one-row tibble with the same core columns as tost_on_lmer_term().
rope_on_brms_term <- function(fit, term, bound, ci = 0.95) {
  stopifnot(inherits(fit, "brmsfit"),
            is.character(term), length(term) == 1,
            is.numeric(bound), length(bound) == 1, is.finite(bound), bound > 0)
  draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit)
  if (!term %in% names(draws)) {
    stop("rope_on_brms_term(): term '", term, "' not among posterior draws. ",
         "Fixed-effect columns: ",
         paste(grep("^b_", names(draws), value = TRUE), collapse = ", "))
  }
  v <- as.numeric(draws[[term]])
  h95 <- as.data.frame(bayestestR::hdi(v, ci = ci))
  h90 <- as.data.frame(bayestestR::hdi(v, ci = 0.90))
  rp  <- as.data.frame(bayestestR::rope(v, range = c(-bound, bound), ci = ci))
  stopifnot(all(c("CI_low", "CI_high") %in% names(h95)),
            "ROPE_Percentage" %in% names(rp))
  inside  <- h95$CI_low > -bound && h95$CI_high < bound
  outside <- h95$CI_high < -bound || h95$CI_low > bound
  fam <- tryCatch(fit$family$family, error = function(e) NA_character_)
  tibble(
    method       = "region of practical equivalence (brms posterior)",
    term         = term,
    scale        = if (identical(fam, "gaussian")) "linear predictor (rating points)"
                   else paste0("linear predictor (", fam, " link scale)"),
    bound_lo     = -bound,
    bound_hi     =  bound,
    estimate     = median(v),
    se           = sd(v),
    df           = NA_real_,
    ci90_lo      = h90$CI_low,
    ci90_hi      = h90$CI_high,
    hdi95_lo     = h95$CI_low,
    hdi95_hi     = h95$CI_high,
    # Probability of direction: the share of the posterior on whichever side
    # of zero the median sits, reported because it is the quantity a reader
    # most often wants beside an interval that includes zero.
    pd           = max(mean(v > 0), mean(v < 0)),
    prop_in_rope_full  = mean(abs(v) < bound),
    prop_in_rope_hdi95 = rp$ROPE_Percentage[1],
    reading      = if (inside) "the 95% interval lies inside this bound"
                   else if (outside) "the 95% interval lies outside this bound"
                   else "the 95% interval straddles an edge of this bound"
  )
}

# ---- The sensitivity grid --------------------------------------------------
# The term is the attribution-by-image-kind interaction: under treatment
# coding it is the difference between the figurative and non-figurative
# penalties, which is the quantity H3 says is zero.
fits_lmer <- list(creativity = creat_fit, effort = eff_fit)
fits_brms <- list(creativity = bayes_creat, effort = bayes_eff)
TERM_INT_LMER <- "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"
TERM_INT_BRMS <- "b_TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"

ROLE_NOTE <- sprintf(
  paste0("descriptive sensitivity; no verdict on H3. The registered bound of ",
         "+/- %.2f rating points is tested in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section ",
         "7.10, under both the intercepts-only and the maximal ",
         "random-effects structures."),
  REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND)

# Each row carries the status of the fit it was read from: the primary lmer
# fit's (section 1) or the Gaussian brms fit's (section 2). A row from a fit
# that is not usable keeps its numbers for inspection and has its reading set
# to NA.
lmer_status <- c(creativity = lmm_fit_status(creat_fit),
                 effort     = lmm_fit_status(eff_fit))

equivalence_sensitivity <- map_dfr(c("creativity", "effort"), function(dm) {
  map_dfr(EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS, function(b) {
    bind_rows(
      tost_on_lmer_term(fits_lmer[[dm]], TERM_INT_LMER, b) %>%
        mutate(source_fit = sprintf("models/study1_lmm_%s.rds", dm),
               fit_status = lmer_status[[dm]]),
      rope_on_brms_term(fits_brms[[dm]], TERM_INT_BRMS, b) %>%
        mutate(source_fit = sprintf("models/study1_brms_primary_%s.rds", dm),
               fit_status = brms_status[[dm]])
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        quantity   = "attribution x image kind interaction on ratings",
        dimension  = dm,
        bound      = b,
        bound_is_registered = FALSE,
        role       = ROLE_NOTE,
        reading    = if_else(fit_status %in% USABLE_STATUS, reading,
                             NA_character_)
      )
  })
}) %>%
  relocate(quantity, dimension, bound, bound_is_registered, role, method,
           source_fit, term, scale, bound_lo, bound_hi, estimate, se, df,
           ci90_lo, ci90_hi, tost_p_low, tost_p_high, tost_p, nhst_p, reading,
           fit_status)

# Every row here is computed from a fit that already exists, so an empty or
# half-filled table is a bug rather than a missing input.
usable_rows <- equivalence_sensitivity$fit_status %in% USABLE_STATUS
stopifnot(
  nrow(equivalence_sensitivity) ==
    2 * length(EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS) * 2,   # dimensions x bounds x methods
  !anyNA(equivalence_sensitivity$estimate),
  !anyNA(equivalence_sensitivity$reading[usable_rows]),
  all(equivalence_sensitivity$bound %in% EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS),
  !any(equivalence_sensitivity$bound_is_registered),
  !anyNA(equivalence_sensitivity$tost_p[
    grepl("^two one-sided", equivalence_sensitivity$method)]),
  !anyNA(equivalence_sensitivity$prop_in_rope_full[
    grepl("^region of practical", equivalence_sensitivity$method)])
)

cat("=== Equivalence sensitivity at the wider bounds (no verdict on H3) ===\n")
print(equivalence_sensitivity %>%
        dplyr::select(dimension, bound, method, estimate, ci90_lo, ci90_hi,
```
