                      tost_p, prop_in_rope_full, reading, fit_status),
      n = Inf, width = Inf)

write_output(equivalence_sensitivity,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv"))
```

**What to look at.** Read the two dimensions separately, and read each bound
as a question rather than as a result. If the interval already sits inside
0.30 on a dimension, the wider bounds add nothing the registered test did not
settle. If it sits inside 0.50 but not 0.30, then the equivalence conclusion
on that dimension depends on how wide a difference one is willing to call
negligible, and the manuscript should say so in those words rather than
quoting a bound at which the conclusion happens to hold.

---

# 4. Sensitivity power analysis

```{r sensitivity-power-v2, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=file_sha256(c(file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_creativity.rds"), file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_effort.rds")))}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DESIGN-SENSITIVITY power analysis (NOT observed or post-hoc power).
#
# The fitted primary LMM supplies the design: its realized N (111
# participants x 10 stimuli) and its estimated variance components
# (participant, stimulus, residual). The coefficient of interest is FIXED at
# a series of hypothesized values, new data are simulated from that model,
# and simr::powerSim counts how often the term is detected at alpha = .05.
# The observed coefficient itself is NOT used as the hypothesized effect, so
# this is not the circular "observed power" (Hoenig & Heisey 2001). The
# question is about the design: what is the smallest coefficient THIS design
# would have detected with 80% power?
#
# Grid and columns.
#   1. The main-effect grid is c(0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55) rating units,
#      wide enough to bracket the 80% threshold the section reports. These
#      rows are about the H1 contrast. simr fixes and tests one named
#      coefficient, and under the treatment coding of the primary fit no
#      single coefficient is the H1 contrast: TypeAI is the attribution
#      effect at the non-figurative images, and the H1 contrast is TypeAI
#      plus half the interaction. sum_coded_fit() therefore refits the
#      primary model with image kind sum-coded (the two kinds coded +1 and
#      -1, so the other coefficients are read at the average of the two
#      kinds). That changes what the coefficients mean and nothing else: the
#      fitted values and the variance components are those of the primary
#      fit, which the function checks. Its TypeAI coefficient
#      is the H1 contrast with the generator-minus-human sign, and the power
#      of a two-sided test does not depend on that sign, so each
#      hypothesized value is the size of the H1 contrast.
#   2. `hypothesized_beta_rating_units` holds RAW rating-scale betas
#      (assigned via fixef(m)[term] <- eff), not Cohen's d (a difference in
#      standard-deviation units). Two implied-d columns accompany it for
#      readers who think in d: beta / sqrt(sum of variance components)
#      (total-SD d, the one that matches the spread of a single rating) and
#      beta / residual sigma (the larger, within-cell d).
#      `estimand` and `coding` say which quantity and which coding each row
#      belongs to.
#   3. The interaction term (TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure) is run at beta =
#      0.20 and 0.30. This is the quantity H3 predicts to be zero. The power
#      on these rows is the power of an ordinary significance test to DETECT
#      an interaction of that size, and it is reported for H3 as descriptive
#      context only. The registered test for H3 is an equivalence test,
#      which asks whether an interaction of the bound's size can be RULED
#      OUT, and the power that decides whether its result is informative is
#      the equivalence test's own power, computed in the next chunk from the
#      same fitted model. These rows use the treatment-coded primary fit,
#      whose interaction coefficient is the difference between the two
#      penalties, the quantity H3 is about. Because the interaction is a
#      within-participant contrast (Satterthwaite df ~ 989), it has far more
#      power for the same beta than the between-participant H1 contrast.
#
# Monte Carlo precision. The power in each cell is a share of simulated
# datasets, so it carries a Monte Carlo standard error: the amount that share
# would wander from one run of the simulation to the next purely because the
# datasets are random draws. nsim = 200 per cell gives MC SE = sqrt(p(1-p)/200)
# <= 0.035 (0.028 at p = .80); reported per row as `mc_se`. Runtime ~10-15
# min for the 14 cells. A cell in which more than 5 per cent of the simulated
# fits errored has `status` saying so and is left out of the 80 per cent
# summary.
#
# The chunk is cached, and cache.extra in the chunk header keys the cache on
# the SHA-256 checksums of the two model files in models/, so a re-run of
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd that changes either file invalidates it rather than
# leaving simulations built on stale variance components in place. The
# tables are written by the uncached chunk that follows, so they are written
# on every run whether this chunk ran or was restored from the cache.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

POWER_NSIM      <- 200
POWER_GRID_MAIN <- c(0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55)  # rating units, H1 contrast
POWER_GRID_INT  <- c(0.20, 0.30)                    # rating units, interaction
POWER_TARGET    <- 0.80
POWER_MAX_FAILED_SHARE <- 0.05

# The primary model refitted with image kind sum-coded, on the rows of the
# primary fit. The sum coding is set on the image-kind factor of the data
# itself, because simr rebuilds the model matrix from the formula and the
# data for every simulated dataset and would not see a contrasts argument
# given to lmer(). The formula is written here, in this function, so that
# simr finds the data in the formula's environment; getData() also attaches
# it to the fit. The checks: the same fitted values and variance components
# as the primary fit, and a TypeAI coefficient equal to minus the H1
# contrast emmeans reads off the primary fit. (The REML log-likelihood
# itself shifts by a constant under a recoding of the fixed effects, log 4
# here, so it is not one of the checks.)
sum_coded_fit <- function(fit, dim_name) {
  dat <- as.data.frame(model.frame(fit))[, c("rating", "Type",
                                             "stimulus_type", "id",
                                             "stimulus_id")]
  contrasts(dat$stimulus_type) <- contr.sum(2)
  refit <- lmerTest::lmer(
    rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data = dat, REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  simr::getData(refit) <- dat
  stopifnot("stimulus_type1" %in% names(fixef(refit)))
  vc_ref <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))$vcov
  vc_sum <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(refit))$vcov
  h1 <- h1_contrast_freq(fit, long %>% filter(dimension == dim_name))
  stopifnot(
    max(abs(fitted(refit) - fitted(fit))) < 1e-6,
    max(abs(vc_sum - vc_ref) / vc_ref) < 1e-4,
    abs(fixef(refit)[["TypeAI"]] + h1$estimate) < 1e-6
  )
  refit
}
power_fits_h1 <- list(creativity = sum_coded_fit(creat_fit, "creativity"),
                      effort     = sum_coded_fit(eff_fit,   "effort"))
power_fits_int <- list(creativity = creat_fit, effort = eff_fit)

ESTIMAND_POWER_H1 <- paste0(
  "H1 contrast (generator minus human, averaged over image kind; a ",
  "two-sided test, so the sign does not matter)")
ESTIMAND_POWER_INT <- paste0(
  "attribution x image kind interaction: figurative penalty minus ",
  "non-figurative penalty")

run_sensitivity <- function(model, dim_name, term, effect_candidates,
                            estimand, coding, nsim = POWER_NSIM) {
  if (!term %in% names(fixef(model))) {
    stop("run_sensitivity(): term '", term, "' not in fixef(model): ",
         paste(names(fixef(model)), collapse = ", "))
  }
  vc       <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))
  sd_total <- sqrt(sum(vc$vcov))     # id + stimulus + residual variance
  sd_resid <- sigma(model)

  map_dfr(effect_candidates, function(eff) {
    m <- model
    fixef(m)[term] <- eff
    ps <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
      simr::powerSim(m, test = fixed(term, "t"), nsim = nsim,
                     progress = FALSE)
    ))
    pw <- ps$x / ps$n
    tibble(
      dimension                      = dim_name,
      term                           = term,
      estimand                       = estimand,
      coding                         = coding,
      hypothesized_beta_rating_units = eff,
      implied_d_total_sd             = eff / sd_total,
      implied_d_residual_sd          = eff / sd_resid,
      power                          = pw,
      ci_lo                          = binom.test(ps$x, ps$n)$conf.int[1],
      ci_hi                          = binom.test(ps$x, ps$n)$conf.int[2],
      mc_se                          = sqrt(pw * (1 - pw) / ps$n),
      nsim                           = ps$n,
      # nrow(NULL) is NULL, and tibble() silently DROPS a NULL column, so a
      # cell with no simr error log would lose this column and bind_rows()
      # would backfill NA. Return 0L explicitly when simr reports no errors.
      # ps$errors is a data.frame in simr 1.0.9 (installed); if that
      # changes, this is NA.
      n_sim_errors                   = tryCatch({
                                          e <- ps$errors
                                          if (is.null(e)) 0L else as.integer(nrow(e))
                                        }, error = function(e) NA_integer_),
      analysis_type                  = "design sensitivity (coefficient fixed; not observed power)"
    ) %>%
      mutate(status = case_when(
        is.na(n_sim_errors) ~ "error count unavailable",
        n_sim_errors > POWER_MAX_FAILED_SHARE * nsim ~
          sprintf("too many failed simulations: %d of %d", n_sim_errors, nsim),
        TRUE ~ "ok"))
  })
}

CODING_SUM <- "image kind sum-coded (refit of the primary model, same fit)"
CODING_TRT <- "treatment coding (the primary fit)"
power_table <- bind_rows(
  run_sensitivity(power_fits_h1$creativity, "creativity", "TypeAI",
                  POWER_GRID_MAIN, ESTIMAND_POWER_H1, CODING_SUM),
  run_sensitivity(power_fits_h1$effort, "effort", "TypeAI",
                  POWER_GRID_MAIN, ESTIMAND_POWER_H1, CODING_SUM),
  run_sensitivity(power_fits_int$creativity, "creativity",
                  "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure", POWER_GRID_INT,
                  ESTIMAND_POWER_INT, CODING_TRT),
  run_sensitivity(power_fits_int$effort, "effort",
                  "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure", POWER_GRID_INT,
                  ESTIMAND_POWER_INT, CODING_TRT)
)
power_table

# Smallest hypothesized beta at which power >= 80%, per dimension x term,
# from the cells whose simulations ran (status "ok"). A curve that does not
# reach the target raises a warning rather than stopping the knit; the
# remedy is to extend the grid, not to read past the warning.
power_80 <- power_table %>%
  filter(status == "ok") %>%
  group_by(dimension, term, estimand, coding) %>%
  summarise(
    max_power_in_grid      = max(power),
    smallest_beta_at_80pct = if (any(power >= POWER_TARGET))
      min(hypothesized_beta_rating_units[power >= POWER_TARGET]) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# The interaction rows are descriptive context for H3, and the role column
# says so on every one of them: the smallest interaction an ordinary
# significance test detects at 80 per cent power is not the quantity that
# decides whether the registered equivalence test is informative. That
# quantity is the equivalence test's own power, computed in the next chunk,
# which also reads the registered verdict and writes the informativeness
# flag. The registered bound (REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, set in the switches
# chunk) is carried on the interaction rows so the two tables can be read
# side by side. Both columns are NA on the TypeAI rows.
H3_INT_TERM <- "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"
power_80 <- power_80 %>%
  mutate(
    h3_registered_bound = if_else(term == H3_INT_TERM,
                                  REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, NA_real_),
    role = if_else(
      term == H3_INT_TERM,
      paste0("descriptive context for H3: the smallest interaction an ",
             "ordinary significance test detects at 80 per cent power; ",
             "carries no verdict. Whether the registered equivalence test ",
             "is informative is decided by its own power, in ",
             "study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv"),
      NA_character_)
  )
print(power_80)
if (any(is.na(power_80$smallest_beta_at_80pct))) {
  warning("Sensitivity grid does not reach ", POWER_TARGET,
          " power for: ",
          paste(with(power_80[is.na(power_80$smallest_beta_at_80pct), ],
                     paste(dimension, term)), collapse = "; "),
          ". Extend POWER_GRID_MAIN / POWER_GRID_INT.")
}
stopifnot(!anyNA(power_table$power))

cat("\n=== H3: the smallest detectable interaction (descriptive context) ===\n")
for (k in which(power_80$term == H3_INT_TERM)) {
  row <- power_80[k, ]
  msg <- if (is.na(row$smallest_beta_at_80pct)) {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "%s: no point of the interaction grid reaches %.0f per cent power ",
      "(the highest power in the grid is %.2f), so the smallest interaction ",
      "a significance test detects lies above %.2f rating points. This is ",
      "descriptive context and carries no verdict on H3."),
      row$dimension, 100 * POWER_TARGET, row$max_power_in_grid,
      max(POWER_GRID_INT))
  } else {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "%s: the smallest interaction an ordinary significance test detects ",
      "at %.0f per cent power is %.2f rating points. This is descriptive ",
      "context and carries no verdict on H3; the registered bound is +/- ",
      "%.2f, and whether the equivalence test at that bound is informative ",
      "is decided by the equivalence test's own power, computed next."),
      row$dimension, 100 * POWER_TARGET, row$smallest_beta_at_80pct,
      row$h3_registered_bound)
  }
  cat(strwrap(msg, width = 78, exdent = 2), sep = "\n")
}

power_computed_at <- Sys.time()
```

```{r sensitivity-power-write}
# Written on every run, from the results above whether they were computed in
# this run or restored from the knitr cache; the run record says which.
log_knitr_cache("sensitivity-power-v2", power_computed_at)
for (k in seq_len(nrow(power_table))) {
  r <- power_table[k, ]
  log_record("fit", sprintf("power simulation, %s, %s at %.2f",
                            r$dimension, r$term,
                            r$hypothesized_beta_rating_units),
             if (r$status == "ok") "ok" else "error", r$status)
}
write_output(power_table,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_sensitivity_power.csv"))
write_output(power_80,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_sensitivity_power_80pct.csv"))
```

**What the design can resolve for H3.** The registered test for H3 is an
equivalence test at the bound of ±0.20 rating points: two one-sided tests,
which pass when the 90 per cent interval on the attribution-by-image-kind
interaction lies inside the bound. The chunk above asks how small an
interaction an ordinary significance test would detect. That is a different
question, because detecting an effect and ruling out an effect of the bound's
size are not the same thing, and its answer does not say whether the
equivalence test could have passed. The quantity that does is the power of the
equivalence test itself: the probability that the 90 per cent interval falls
inside the bound when the true interaction is zero. The chunk below computes it
by simulation from the same fitted model, at the registered bound and the two
wider ones of section 3, under a true interaction of zero and, as sensitivity,
of 0.10 rating points, and reads it against the registered verdict.

The reading rule has one asymmetry, and it is the reason a pass and a fail are
treated differently. A pass is valid evidence whatever the test's power,
because the two one-sided tests hold the rate of wrongly declaring equivalence
at 5 per cent on each side (Lakens 2017); low power only makes a pass unlikely,
not wrong. A fail is informative only when the design would usually have passed
under a true zero. When that power is below 80 per cent, a fail says more about
the width of the interval than about the interaction, and is reported as
uninformative.

```{r h3-equivalence-power, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=file_sha256(c(file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_creativity.rds"), file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_effort.rds"), file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h3_equivalence.csv")))}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POWER OF THE EQUIVALENCE TEST for H3 (design sensitivity, NOT observed /
# post-hoc power).
#
# WHAT IS ASKED. The registered test for H3 is two one-sided tests at the
# bound of +/- 0.20 rating points on the attribution-by-image-kind
# interaction (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10): it passes when the 90 per
# cent interval on that term lies inside the bound. Its power is the
# probability of passing when the true interaction is zero. That is the
# quantity that says whether this design could have resolved the bound, and
# it is not the detection power of the chunk above: a design can detect an
# interaction of 0.30 with high probability and still, under a true zero,
# produce a 90 per cent interval wider than +/- 0.20 most of the time. The
# same simulation is run with the true interaction at 0.10 rating points as
# sensitivity, and every interval is read against the registered bound and
# the two wider ones of section 3, so the table also says how far the bound
# would have to be widened before the design usually passed.
#
# WHAT IS SIMULATED. The same machinery as the chunk above, called directly.
# simr::doSim() draws a new set of ratings from the primary model's formula
# with its fitted variance components (participant, image, residual) and
# its fixed effects, the interaction having been set to the true value under
# study; new participant and image effects are drawn on every dataset, so
# each dataset is a new sample of this design. simr::doFit() then re-runs
# the model's own fitting call on the simulated ratings, so the refit is the
# primary model fitted the way section 7 of Study1_01_Quant.Rmd fits it,
# with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom available. The 90 per cent interval
# is taken from tost_on_lmer_term() of section 3, the helper that runs the
# two one-sided tests on the real data, so the decision rule is the same
# code. One fit serves all three bounds: whether the interval lies inside
# 0.20, 0.30 and 0.50 is read off the same interval.
#
# WHAT IS REPORTED, one row per dimension, true interaction and bound.
#   equivalence_power   the share of datasets on which the 90 per cent
#                       interval lies inside the bound, which is the power
#                       of the two one-sided tests at that bound under that
#                       true interaction. mc_se is its Monte Carlo standard
#                       error, sqrt(p(1 - p) / n_used), the amount the share
#                       would wander from one run of the simulation to the
#                       next purely because the datasets are random draws;
#                       ci_lo and ci_hi are the exact binomial interval.
#   analytic_power      the same probability worked out without simulation
#                       from the standard error the registered test
#                       deposited. With the standard error held at that
#                       value, the estimate is normal around the true
#                       interaction, and the interval lies inside the bound
#                       exactly when the estimate is within (bound minus the
#                       interval's half-width) of zero. It is printed beside
#                       the simulated value as a check on both.
#   mean_estimate, sd_estimate, mean_se
#                       the average and spread of the simulated estimates
#                       and the average of their standard errors. The
#                       average should sit at the true interaction and the
#                       spread should match the standard error; a gap means
#                       the simulation is not generating what it claims.
#   n_singular, n_failed, n_warnings
#                       how many refits were singular (in this
#                       intercepts-only model, the participant or the image
#                       variance estimated at zero; the interval is still
#                       valid and the dataset is kept), how many errored (set
#                       aside), and how many raised an optimizer warning
#                       (kept, counted).
#   status              "ok" for a cell in which at least 95 per cent of the
#                       refits ran; otherwise it says how many ran, and the
#                       cell's power and interval are NA, because a share
#                       computed from the datasets that happened to fit is
#                       not the power of the design.
#   registered_test_passed, h3_equivalence_informative
#                       the verdict of the registered test, read from
#                       tables/study1_h3_equivalence.csv on the structure
#                       that carries it, and the flag that governs how the
#                       verdict is reported. A PASS is always informative:
#                       the two one-sided tests hold the rate of wrongly
#                       declaring equivalence at alpha on each side whatever
#                       their power, so a pass is valid evidence on its own
#                       terms, and low power only makes a pass unlikely. A
#                       FAIL is informative only when the power at the
#                       registered bound under a true zero reaches 80 per
#                       cent; below that, the design would usually have
#                       failed even if the two penalties were identical, and
#                       the fail is reported as uninformative. The flag is
#                       one value per dimension, repeated on every row of
#                       that dimension, and it is NA on a fail whose
#                       registered-bound cell did not complete.
#
# Monte Carlo precision: n_sim = 1000 per cell gives a standard error on a
# share of at most sqrt(0.25 / 1000) = 0.016. Two dimensions and two true
# interactions make 4 cells, 4000 simulated datasets and 4000 refits, about
# six hundredths of a second each, so the chunk runs in roughly four
# minutes; the elapsed time is printed at the end. The seed is the
# notebook's, 20260421, and every dataset receives its own seed drawn once
# from it, as in section 4.1, so the run is reproducible dataset by dataset.
#
# The chunk is cached, and cache.extra keys the cache on the SHA-256 checksums
# of the two model files and of the deposited H3 table, so a re-run of
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd that changes any of them invalidates it rather than
# leaving a flag built on a stale verdict in place. The table is written by
# the uncached chunk that follows.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

H3_POW_SEED     <- 20260421
H3_POW_NSIM     <- 1000
H3_POW_TRUE_INT <- c(0, 0.10)                           # rating units
H3_POW_BOUNDS   <- c(REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS)
H3_POW_ALPHA    <- 0.05                                 # each one-sided test
H3_POW_TARGET   <- 0.80
H3_POW_MIN_USED <- 0.95                                 # share of refits
H3_POW_DIMS     <- c("creativity", "effort")
h3_fits         <- list(creativity = creat_fit, effort = eff_fit)
h3_power_path   <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv")
h3_table_path   <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h3_equivalence.csv")
stopifnot(all(H3_POW_BOUNDS > 0), !any(duplicated(H3_POW_BOUNDS)),
          exists("tost_on_lmer_term"), exists("H3_INT_TERM"),
          all(map_lgl(h3_fits, ~ H3_INT_TERM %in% names(fixef(.x)))))

# ---- The registered verdict, one row per dimension -------------------------
# The rule of Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10: the verdict rests on both
# random-effects structures when both are available and the maximal fit is
# not singular, and on the intercepts-only structure alone otherwise;
# h3_structure_used says which. "Passed" means the two one-sided tests at the
# registered bound concluded equivalence on every structure that carries the
# verdict. The deposited standard error and degrees of freedom of the
# intercepts-only fit are read from the same table for the analytic
# approximation and checked against the model file, so the two inputs cannot
# drift apart. If the table is absent, the intercepts-only test is recomputed
# here from the model file and the verdict_source column says so.
if (file.exists(h3_table_path)) {
  h3_dep <- read_csv(h3_table_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("dimension", "random_structure", "bound_role", "equivalent",
                  "se", "df", "h3_claim", "h3_structure_used") %in%
                  names(h3_dep)))
  h3_verdict <- h3_dep %>%
    filter(bound_role == "registered") %>%
    group_by(dimension) %>%
    summarise(
      h3_structure_used = first(h3_structure_used),
      h3_claim          = first(h3_claim),
      se_deposited      = se[grepl("^intercepts", random_structure)][1],
      df_deposited      = df[grepl("^intercepts", random_structure)][1],
      registered_test_passed =
        if (grepl("^intercepts only", first(h3_structure_used)))
          equivalent[grepl("^intercepts", random_structure)][1] %in% TRUE
        else all(equivalent %in% TRUE),
      verdict_source    = "tables/study1_h3_equivalence.csv (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10)",
      .groups = "drop")
} else {
  message("tables/study1_h3_equivalence.csv not found; the registered ",
          "verdict is recomputed from the intercepts-only fits alone.")
  h3_verdict <- map_dfr(H3_POW_DIMS, function(dm) {
    tt <- tost_on_lmer_term(h3_fits[[dm]], H3_INT_TERM,
                            REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, alpha = H3_POW_ALPHA)
    tibble(dimension         = dm,
           h3_structure_used = "intercepts only; recomputed here because the deposited table is absent",
           h3_claim          = NA_character_,
           se_deposited      = tt$se,
           df_deposited      = tt$df,
           registered_test_passed = tt$tost_p < H3_POW_ALPHA,
           verdict_source    = "recomputed from models/study1_lmm_<dimension>.rds; tables/study1_h3_equivalence.csv absent")
  })
}
stopifnot(setequal(h3_verdict$dimension, H3_POW_DIMS),
          !anyNA(h3_verdict$se_deposited), !anyNA(h3_verdict$df_deposited),
          !anyNA(h3_verdict$registered_test_passed))
for (dm in H3_POW_DIMS) {
  se_fit <- summary(h3_fits[[dm]])$coefficients[H3_INT_TERM, "Std. Error"]
  se_dep <- h3_verdict$se_deposited[h3_verdict$dimension == dm]
  if (abs(se_fit - se_dep) > 1e-6) {
    stop("h3-equivalence-power: the deposited standard error for ", dm,
         " (", signif(se_dep, 6), ") differs from the model file's (",
         signif(se_fit, 6), "). Re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd so the H3 table ",
         "and models/ agree.")
  }
}

# ---- The analytic approximation ---------------------------------------------
# With the standard error held at its deposited value, the estimate is
# normal around the true interaction, and the 90 per cent interval is the
# estimate plus or minus qt(1 - alpha, df) times the standard error. The
# interval lies inside the bound exactly when the estimate lies within
# (bound minus that half-width) of zero; when the half-width exceeds the
# bound the interval can never fit and the power is zero.
h3_analytic_power <- function(bound, true_int, se, df, alpha = H3_POW_ALPHA) {
  half <- qt(1 - alpha, df) * se
  if (bound <= half) return(0)
  pnorm((bound - half - true_int) / se) - pnorm((-bound + half - true_int) / se)
}

# ---- One simulated dataset, its refit, and its 90 per cent interval ---------
# model_true is the primary fit with the interaction set to the true value.
# Warnings are counted and muffled rather than printed, as in section 4.1.
fit_one_h3 <- function(sim_seed, model_true) {
  set.seed(sim_seed)
  n_warn <- 0L
  result <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch({
      y   <- simr::doSim(model_true)
      fit <- simr::doFit(y, model_true)
      tt  <- tost_on_lmer_term(fit, H3_INT_TERM, REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND,
                               alpha = H3_POW_ALPHA)
      tibble(estimate = tt$estimate, se = tt$se, df = tt$df,
             ci90_lo  = tt$ci90_lo, ci90_hi = tt$ci90_hi,
             singular = lme4::isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-4),
             failed   = FALSE, err = NA_character_)
    }, error = function(e) {
      tibble(estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
             ci90_lo = NA_real_, ci90_hi = NA_real_, singular = NA,
             failed = TRUE, err = conditionMessage(e))
    }),
    warning = function(w) {
      n_warn <<- n_warn + 1L
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
  result %>% mutate(sim_seed = sim_seed, n_warnings = n_warn)
}

# ---- One cell: n_sim datasets at one dimension and one true interaction ----
# Returns one row per bound. The rows of a cell share their fits: the same
# intervals are read against each bound in turn.
run_h3_cell <- function(dim_name, true_int, seeds) {
  model_true <- h3_fits[[dim_name]]
  fixef(model_true)[H3_INT_TERM] <- true_int
  sims <- map_dfr(seeds, fit_one_h3, model_true = model_true)
  ok   <- sims %>% filter(!failed, is.finite(ci90_lo), is.finite(ci90_hi))
  v    <- h3_verdict[h3_verdict$dimension == dim_name, ]
  cell_ok <- nrow(ok) >= H3_POW_MIN_USED * length(seeds)
  map_dfr(H3_POW_BOUNDS, function(b) {
    n_in <- sum(ok$ci90_lo > -b & ok$ci90_hi < b)
    pw   <- if (cell_ok) n_in / nrow(ok) else NA_real_
    bt   <- if (cell_ok) binom.test(n_in, nrow(ok))$conf.int else
              c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    tibble(
      dimension           = dim_name,
      true_interaction    = true_int,
      bound               = b,
      bound_is_registered = isTRUE(all.equal(b, REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND)),
      n_sim               = length(seeds),
      n_used              = nrow(ok),
      n_failed            = sum(sims$failed),
      n_singular          = sum(sims$singular %in% TRUE),
      n_warnings          = sum(sims$n_warnings),
      n_inside            = n_in,
      equivalence_power   = pw,
      mc_se               = sqrt(pw * (1 - pw) / nrow(ok)),
      ci_lo               = bt[1],
      ci_hi               = bt[2],
      analytic_power      = h3_analytic_power(b, true_int, v$se_deposited,
                                              v$df_deposited),
      se_deposited        = v$se_deposited,
      df_deposited        = v$df_deposited,
      halfwidth_90        = qt(1 - H3_POW_ALPHA, v$df_deposited) *
                            v$se_deposited,
      mean_estimate       = mean(ok$estimate),
      sd_estimate         = sd(ok$estimate),
      mean_se             = mean(ok$se),
      alpha_per_side      = H3_POW_ALPHA,
      status              = if (cell_ok) "ok" else
                              sprintf("too many failed refits: %d of %d used",
                                      nrow(ok), length(seeds))
    )
  })
}

# ---- The cells, in a fixed order, each with its own block of seeds ---------
h3_cells <- expand_grid(dimension        = H3_POW_DIMS,
                        true_interaction = H3_POW_TRUE_INT)
set.seed(H3_POW_SEED)
h3_seed_pool <- sample.int(.Machine$integer.max,
                           size = nrow(h3_cells) * H3_POW_NSIM)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(h3_seed_pool)))

h3_t0 <- Sys.time()
h3_equiv_power <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(h3_cells)), function(k) {
  cell  <- h3_cells[k, ]
  seeds <- h3_seed_pool[((k - 1) * H3_POW_NSIM + 1):(k * H3_POW_NSIM)]
  cat(sprintf("H3 equivalence power: %-10s true interaction %.2f ... ",
              cell$dimension, cell$true_interaction))
  rows <- run_h3_cell(cell$dimension, cell$true_interaction, seeds)
  cat(sprintf("done (%d used, %d singular, %d failed, %d warnings)\n",
              rows$n_used[1], rows$n_singular[1], rows$n_failed[1],
              rows$n_warnings[1]))
  rows
})
h3_elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), h3_t0, units = "mins"))
cat(sprintf("H3 equivalence power simulation: %d cells x %d datasets in %.1f minutes\n",
            nrow(h3_cells), H3_POW_NSIM, h3_elapsed))

# ---- The flag, one per dimension, from the registered bound under zero -----
h3_flag <- h3_equiv_power %>%
  filter(bound_is_registered, true_interaction == 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(dimension,
                power_registered_bound_true_zero = equivalence_power,
                power_registered_bound_true_zero_mc_se = mc_se,
                analytic_registered_bound_true_zero = analytic_power) %>%
  left_join(h3_verdict, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(
    h3_equivalence_informative = case_when(
      registered_test_passed                   ~ TRUE,
      is.na(power_registered_bound_true_zero)  ~ NA,
      TRUE ~ power_registered_bound_true_zero >= H3_POW_TARGET),
    informative_rule = paste0(
      "a pass is informative whatever the power, because the two one-sided ",
      "tests hold the rate of wrongly declaring equivalence at alpha per ",
      "side; a fail is informative only when the power of the equivalence ",
      "test at the registered bound under a true interaction of zero is at ",
      "least ", H3_POW_TARGET),
    power_target = H3_POW_TARGET
  )
stopifnot(nrow(h3_flag) == length(H3_POW_DIMS))
if (anyNA(h3_flag$h3_equivalence_informative)) {
  warning("H3 equivalence power: the registered-bound cell did not complete ",
          "for ", paste(h3_flag$dimension[is.na(h3_flag$h3_equivalence_informative)],
                        collapse = ", "),
          "; h3_equivalence_informative is NA there.")
}

h3_equiv_power <- h3_equiv_power %>%
  left_join(h3_flag %>%
              dplyr::select(dimension, registered_test_passed, h3_claim,
                            h3_structure_used, verdict_source,
                            power_registered_bound_true_zero,
                            h3_equivalence_informative, informative_rule,
                            power_target),
            by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(seed                      = H3_POW_SEED,
         runtime_minutes_all_cells = h3_elapsed,
         analysis_type             = paste0(
           "design sensitivity: power of the two one-sided tests at the ",
           "stated bound under the stated true interaction; not observed ",
           "power")) %>%
  relocate(dimension, true_interaction, bound, bound_is_registered,
           equivalence_power, mc_se, ci_lo, ci_hi, analytic_power)

# Checks. Every cell ran from a fit that exists, so an empty or half-filled
# table is a bug rather than a missing input; a cell with too many failed
# refits is recorded in its status column instead. Among the cells that
# completed, the intervals are read against nested bounds, so the share
# inside can only rise with the bound, and the simulated estimates should
# average to the true interaction; a gap wider than 0.02 rating points
# (several times the Monte Carlo standard error of that average) means the
# coefficient was not set as intended.
h3_done <- h3_equiv_power %>% filter(status == "ok")
h3_monotone <- h3_done %>%
  group_by(dimension, true_interaction) %>%
  arrange(bound, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(ok = all(diff(equivalence_power) >= 0), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(
  nrow(h3_equiv_power) == nrow(h3_cells) * length(H3_POW_BOUNDS),
  !anyNA(h3_done$equivalence_power),
  all(h3_monotone$ok),
  all(abs(h3_done$mean_estimate - h3_done$true_interaction) < 0.02)
)
if (any(h3_equiv_power$status != "ok")) {
  warning("H3 equivalence power: ", sum(h3_equiv_power$status != "ok"),
          " rows come from cells with too many failed refits; their power ",
          "is NA.")
}

cat("\n=== H3: power of the equivalence test, by bound and true interaction ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h3_equiv_power %>%
  dplyr::select(dimension, true_interaction, bound, equivalence_power, mc_se,
                ci_lo, ci_hi, analytic_power, mean_estimate, sd_estimate,
                n_singular, n_failed, n_warnings) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3)))))

# The registered reading in words, one per dimension. The detection figure
# from the chunk above is quoted at the end of each as context.
cat("\n=== H3: the registered reading ===\n")
for (dm in H3_POW_DIMS) {
  f   <- h3_flag[h3_flag$dimension == dm, ]
  ctx <- power_80 %>% filter(dimension == dm, term == H3_INT_TERM)
  claim_txt <- if (is.na(f$h3_claim)) {
    "verdict recomputed here from the intercepts-only fit"
  } else f$h3_claim
  ctx_txt <- if (nrow(ctx) == 1 && !is.na(ctx$smallest_beta_at_80pct)) {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "The smallest interaction an ordinary significance test detects at ",
      "%.0f per cent power, %.2f rating points, is descriptive context and ",
      "carries no verdict."), 100 * POWER_TARGET, ctx$smallest_beta_at_80pct)
  } else {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "The detection grid did not locate the smallest interaction a ",
      "significance test detects at %.0f per cent power; that figure is ",
      "descriptive context in any case and carries no verdict."),
      100 * POWER_TARGET)
  }
  msg <- if (f$registered_test_passed) {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "%s: the registered equivalence test at +/- %.2f rating points passed ",
      "(structure: %s; verdict: %s). A pass is informative whatever the ",
      "test's power, because the two one-sided tests hold the rate of ",
      "wrongly declaring equivalence at %.0f per cent on each side, so ",
      "h3_equivalence_informative is TRUE and the verdict is read on its own ",
      "terms. For the record, the power of that test under a true ",
      "interaction of zero is %.2f (Monte Carlo SE %.3f; analytic ",
      "approximation %.2f)."),
      dm, REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, f$h3_structure_used, claim_txt,
      100 * H3_POW_ALPHA, f$power_registered_bound_true_zero,
      f$power_registered_bound_true_zero_mc_se,
      f$analytic_registered_bound_true_zero)
  } else if (is.na(f$h3_equivalence_informative)) {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "%s: the registered equivalence test at +/- %.2f rating points did not ",
      "pass (structure: %s; verdict: %s). The power simulation at the ",
      "registered bound did not complete, so h3_equivalence_informative is ",
      "NA and the fail carries no reading on informativeness."),
      dm, REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, f$h3_structure_used, claim_txt)
  } else if (isTRUE(f$h3_equivalence_informative)) {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "%s: the registered equivalence test at +/- %.2f rating points did not ",
      "pass (structure: %s; verdict: %s). Its power under a true interaction ",
      "of zero is %.2f (Monte Carlo SE %.3f; analytic approximation %.2f), at ",
      "or above %.0f per cent, so the fail is informative: a design that ",
      "would usually have passed under a true zero did not, and the verdict ",
      "is read on its own terms. h3_equivalence_informative is TRUE."),
      dm, REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, f$h3_structure_used, claim_txt,
      f$power_registered_bound_true_zero,
      f$power_registered_bound_true_zero_mc_se,
      f$analytic_registered_bound_true_zero, 100 * H3_POW_TARGET)
  } else {
    sprintf(paste0(
      "%s: the registered equivalence test at +/- %.2f rating points did not ",
      "pass (structure: %s; verdict: %s). Its power under a true interaction ",
      "of zero is %.2f (Monte Carlo SE %.3f; analytic approximation %.2f), ",
      "below %.0f per cent, so the fail is reported as uninformative: the ",
      "design would usually have failed to pass this bound even if the two ",
      "penalties were identical, and the verdict says more about the width ",
      "of the interval than about the interaction. h3_equivalence_informative ",
      "is FALSE."),
      dm, REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND, f$h3_structure_used, claim_txt,
      f$power_registered_bound_true_zero,
      f$power_registered_bound_true_zero_mc_se,
      f$analytic_registered_bound_true_zero, 100 * H3_POW_TARGET)
  }
  cat(strwrap(paste(msg, ctx_txt), width = 78, exdent = 2), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}

h3_computed_at <- Sys.time()
```

```{r h3-equivalence-power-write}
# Written on every run, from the results above whether they were computed in
# this run or restored from the knitr cache; the run record says which.
log_knitr_cache("h3-equivalence-power", h3_computed_at)
for (k in seq_len(nrow(h3_cells))) {
  cell <- h3_equiv_power %>%
    filter(dimension == h3_cells$dimension[k],
           true_interaction == h3_cells$true_interaction[k])
  log_record("fit", sprintf("H3 equivalence power, %s, true interaction %.2f",
                            cell$dimension[1], cell$true_interaction[1]),
             if (cell$status[1] == "ok") "ok" else "error",
             sprintf("%d of %d refits used; %d singular, %d failed, %d warnings",
                     cell$n_used[1], cell$n_sim[1], cell$n_singular[1],
                     cell$n_failed[1], cell$n_warnings[1]))
}
write_output(h3_equiv_power, h3_power_path)
```

**What to look at.** Read the rows with `true_interaction` 0 and `bound` 0.20
first: that is the power of the registered test, and `analytic_power` beside
it should agree to within the Monte Carlo standard error. Then read the flag.
On a dimension where the test passed, the flag is TRUE and the power is a
record, not a qualification. On a dimension where it did not pass, a power
below 80 per cent means the inconclusive verdict is a fact about the width of
the interval this design produces, not about the interaction, and the
manuscript should say so in those words. The rows at 0.30 and 0.50 say how far
the bound would have to be widened before the design usually passed under a
true zero; they are descriptive, like the wider bounds of section 3, and carry
no verdict.

## 4.1 What the design can resolve for H4

The preregistration asks, under "What the design can resolve", for two
quantities. The first concerns H3: the power of the registered equivalence
test under a true attribution-by-image-kind interaction of zero. The
simulation of section 4 produces it and reads it against the registered
verdict, with the smallest interaction a significance test would detect
reported beside it as context. The second concerns H4, the prediction that
the attribution label changes what a rating is a property of. Under generator
attribution the spread *between* participants should be larger than under
human attribution, and the spread *within* a participant, from one image to
the next, smaller.
H4 is decided by two variance ratios, each the AI arm's variance over the
human arm's and each estimated in `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd` section 7.8.2. The
between-participant ratio is predicted to be above 1. The residual ratio is
predicted to be below 1; the residual is the part of a rating's spread left
once participant and image differences are removed. H4 is supported only when
both predictions hold and each ratio's confidence interval excludes 1. The two
ratios come from different models in `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd`. The
between-participant ratio comes from a crossed model (participants and images
as two separate random factors) that keeps the image random effects and holds
one residual variance for both arms. The residual ratio comes from a model
that lets the residual variance differ by arm and has no image random effect.
The preregistration's design-resolution question concerns the first of the
two. It words the quantity as the expected width of the confidence interval
on the between-participant ratio at 55 and 56 participants per arm.

What the simulation below reports is the spread of the ratio estimate across
simulated datasets: how far the estimated between-participant ratio moves
from one simulated sample of this size to the next. That is a statement
about the precision of the estimator, and it is not the width of a
confidence interval, nor the coverage of one (how often an interval contains
the true ratio); those would need an interval built inside every simulated
dataset, which this simulation does not do. For a skewed quantity such as a
variance ratio the two need not agree.

`simr::powerSim` cannot answer the question, because it fixes a coefficient
and asks how often it is detected. The quantity here is a variance, and what
is wanted is the spread of its estimate, not a detection rate. The simulation
below is therefore written out in full. It generates rating data with the
realized design and the variance components estimated inside each arm, fits
the same two models section 7.8.2 fits, and records how the estimated ratio
scatters over repeated samples of this size. It also records the share of
simulations in which the likelihood-ratio test rejects. When the arms truly
share one variance, that share is the test's false-positive rate; when they
do not, it is the test's power. A short grid of true ratios says which ratios
this design could have detected at 80 per cent power. As in section 4, this
is design resolution, not observed power: the grid does not use the observed
ratio as the hypothesized one.

```{r h4-resolution, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=file_sha256(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_partition.csv"))}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DESIGN-RESOLUTION simulation for H4 (NOT observed / post-hoc power).
#
# WHAT IS SIMULATED. Each simulated dataset has the realized design: 56
# participants told a person made the work and 55 told a generator did, each
# rating the same 10 images (5 figurative, 5 non-figurative) once. One rating
# is built as
#
#     rating = grand mean + participant effect + image effect + remainder
#
# with each of the three random parts drawn from a normal distribution whose
# variance is the one estimated for that arm by the variance partition of
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8.1 (tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv).
# Those six components come from the per-arm intercept-only partition of
# section 7.8.1, not from the registered fit of section 7.8.2: the registered
# fit holds one image variance and one residual variance across the two arms
# and estimates the pair of between-participant variances alongside the fixed
# effects, so its between-participant ratio (the one deposited in
# tables/study1_h4_variance_test.csv) is not the ratio the partition gives
# (the true_ratio_between of the "observed" rows below); the two differ by a
# few percent. The per-arm partition was chosen so that each arm's image and
# remainder variances keep their own values in the simulation; the two
# ratios are printed side by side when the test table is on disk.
# A variance component is the share of the spread in the ratings that one
# source accounts for: the participant effect carries the arm's
# between-participant variance (how much people differ from each other on
# average), the image effect the arm's between-image variance (how much the
# ten pictures differ from each other), and the remainder the arm's
# person-by-image variance (the part specific to one person seeing one
# picture, which also holds any measurement noise). The image effect is one
# draw per image, shared by both arms and scaled by each arm's image standard
# deviation, because both arms saw the same ten pictures and a picture that
# stands out in one arm should stand out in the other. No fixed effects are
# simulated: the grand mean is the only systematic term, because the quantity
# under study is a variance. The fitted models below still carry
# Type * stimulus_type exactly as section 7.8.2 does, so the estimator applied
# to the simulated data is the one applied to the real data.
#
# The simulated ratings are left continuous rather than rounded onto the
# five-point scale. What is being asked is how precisely the model of section
# 7.8.2 can estimate a variance ratio from this many participants; rounding
# and clipping would change the variances the simulation is meant to
# hold fixed, and would turn the answer into a statement about a different
# model.
#
# THE SETTINGS, run separately for creativity and for effort.
#   (i)   the null: both arms share one between-participant variance, the
#         participant-weighted average of the two arms' estimates (56 and 55
#         participants). The between-image and remainder variances keep their
#         observed per-arm values, so the precision of each arm's estimate is
#         the realistic one. Under this setting the share of likelihood-ratio
#         rejections is the test's false-positive rate. That rate is worth
#         reading rather than assuming: the fitted model holds one remainder
#         variance for both arms while the simulated remainder differs by
#         arm, as it does in the data, so the rate is not guaranteed to sit
#         at exactly .05, and the deposited number is what to compare to .05.
#   (ii)  the observed values: every component at its per-arm estimate from
#         section 7.8.1, so the true ratio is the partition's, not the
#         registered test's, for the reason given above. The rejection share
#         here is the power the design has against a true ratio equal to the
#         one the partition observed. It is reported because the
#         preregistration asks what the design can resolve, and is not to be
#         read as the power of the test that was run on the real data.
#   (iii) a grid of true between-participant ratios, 1.25, 1.5, 2 and 3, with
#         the human arm's variance held at its observed value and the AI arm's
#         set to that value times the ratio, the other components as in (ii).
#         This is what says which ratios the design could have detected at 80
#         per cent power, in the same design-sensitivity sense as section 4.
#
# WHAT IS FITTED. To each simulated dataset, the two models of section 7.8.2:
# the primary structure, which holds one between-participant variance common
# to both arms,
#
#     rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
#
# and the arm-specific structure, in which the two indicator columns
# (Human_indicator is 1 for a row from the human arm and 0 otherwise,
# AI_indicator the reverse) give each arm its own between-participant
# variance,
#
#     rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (0 + Human_indicator | id)
#                                    + (0 + AI_indicator | id)
#                                    + (1 | stimulus_id)
#
# Both are fitted by restricted maximum likelihood (which estimates the
# variance components after removing the part of the data the fixed effects
# explain) with the optimizer settings section 7.8.2 uses, and compared by
# the likelihood-ratio test on 1 degree of
# freedom against the ordinary chi-square, for the reason given there: the
# null equates two positive variances, an interior point of the parameter
# space, so the boundary-corrected mixture that applies when a variance is
# tested against zero does not apply. From the arm-specific fit the estimated
# ratio, AI over Human, is kept on the log scale, where the sampling
# distribution of a ratio is close to symmetric, and converted back to a
# ratio for reporting.
#
# WHAT IS REPORTED, one row per dimension and setting.
#   sd_log_ratio         the standard deviation of the estimated log ratio
#                        across simulations, which is the sampling standard
#                        error of the log ratio at this sample size.
#   ratio_q025, ratio_q975, ratio_spread_95
#                        the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the estimated
#                        ratio across simulations, and the distance between
#                        them: the spread of the ratio estimate across
#                        simulated datasets, which says how far the estimate
#                        moves from one sample of this size to the next. It
#                        is not the width of a confidence interval and says
#                        nothing about any interval's coverage: no interval
#                        is computed inside a simulated dataset, and for a
#                        skewed quantity such as a variance ratio the spread
#                        of the estimate and the width of an interval need
#                        not agree. log_ratio_spread_95 is the same distance
#                        on the log scale, on which the spread depends less
#                        on where the true ratio sits. spread_meaning carries
#                        this definition into the deposited file.
#   median_ratio         the median estimated ratio, to be read against
#                        true_ratio_between: the gap between them is the
#                        small-sample bias of the estimator.
#   lrt_reject_rate      the share of simulations in which the
#                        likelihood-ratio test rejects at .05, with its Monte
#                        Carlo standard error, sqrt(p(1 - p) / n_used): the
#                        amount that share would wander from one run of the
#                        simulation to the next purely because the datasets
#                        are random draws.
#   n_singular, n_failed, n_nonfinite_ratio, n_warnings
#                        how many arm-specific fits were singular (a variance
#                        estimated at zero, which may be the image variance
#                        or one arm's between-participant variance; only the
#                        second makes the ratio zero or infinite, and those
#                        datasets are counted again under n_nonfinite_ratio),
#                        how many errored, how many gave a ratio that is not
#                        a finite number, and how many raised an optimizer
#                        warning. The summaries above are computed on the
#                        finite ratios (n_used) and these counts say how many
#                        datasets were set aside.
#   status               "run" for a cell in which at least 95 per cent of
#                        the datasets gave a finite ratio; otherwise it says
#                        how many did, and the cell's summaries and rejection
#                        share are NA.
#   smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct
#                        the smallest ratio in the grid at which the rejection
#                        share reaches 80 per cent, repeated on every row of
#                        that dimension; NA when the grid does not reach it.
#
# Monte Carlo precision: n_sim = 1000 per cell gives a standard error on a
# rejection share of at most sqrt(0.25 / 1000) = 0.016. Two settings and the
# four-point grid make 6 cells per dimension, 12 in all: 12,000 simulated
# datasets and 24,000 lmer fits. A pair of fits takes about three hundredths
# of a second, so the chunk runs in roughly six minutes; the elapsed time is
# printed at the end. The seed is the notebook's, 20260421, and every
# simulated dataset receives its own seed drawn once from it, so the run is
# reproducible dataset by dataset and does not depend on the order in which
# cells are run.
#
# If tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv is not on disk, the simulation
# is skipped and a one-row ledger saying so is written to the same output
# file, in the way section 8 writes its failure ledger even when nothing
# failed, so a downstream reader finds a file with a status column rather
# than nothing.
#
# The chunk is cached, and cache.extra in the chunk header keys the cache on
# the SHA-256 checksum of that partition table, so a re-run of section 7.8.1
# that changes it invalidates the cache rather than leaving simulations built
# on stale components in place. The table is written by the uncached chunk
# that follows.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

H4_RES_SEED         <- 20260421
H4_RES_NSIM         <- 1000
H4_RES_N_HUMAN      <- 56
H4_RES_N_AI         <- 55
H4_RES_N_IMAGES     <- 10
H4_RES_RATIO_GRID   <- c(1.25, 1.5, 2, 3)
H4_RES_POWER_TARGET <- 0.80
H4_RES_ALPHA        <- 0.05
H4_RES_MIN_USED     <- 0.95   # share of datasets with a finite ratio
H4_RES_DIMS         <- c("creativity", "effort")
H4_RES_COMPONENTS   <- c("between images", "between participants",
                         "person-by-image remainder")
# The optimizer settings of section 7.8.2, so the fits are the same fits.
H4_RES_CTRL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

h4_partition_path  <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_partition.csv")
h4_resolution_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_resolution.csv")

if (!file.exists(h4_partition_path)) {

  message("tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv not found; the H4 ",
          "resolution simulation is skipped. Run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd ",
          "section 7.8.1 first.")
  h4_resolution <- tibble(
    dimension = NA_character_,
    setting   = NA_character_,
    status    = "skipped",
    note      = paste("tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv not found;",
                      "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8.1 first")
  )

} else {

  # ---- The variance components, one triple per arm and dimension ----------
  h4_vc <- read_csv(h4_partition_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("dimension", "Type", "component", "variance") %in%
                  names(h4_vc)))
  h4_vc_use <- expand_grid(dimension = H4_RES_DIMS,
                           Type      = c("Human", "AI"),
                           component = H4_RES_COMPONENTS) %>%
    left_join(h4_vc %>% dplyr::select(dimension, Type, component, variance),
              by = c("dimension", "Type", "component"))
  if (anyNA(h4_vc_use$variance) || any(h4_vc_use$variance < 0)) {
    stop("study1_h4_variance_partition.csv is missing a component or holds ",
         "a negative variance; the H4 resolution simulation needs all ",
         "twelve components. Re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8.1.")
  }

  # The registered test's between-participant ratio, read from
  # tables/study1_h4_variance_test.csv when that table is on disk, printed
  # beside the partition's ratio so the gap between the two sits on the page
  # and not only in the comment above.
  h4_test_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_test.csv")
  if (file.exists(h4_test_path)) {
    h4_ratio_compare <- read_csv(h4_test_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::select(dimension,
                    registered_test_ratio = ratio_between_AI_over_Human) %>%
      left_join(
        h4_vc_use %>%
          filter(component == "between participants") %>%
          dplyr::select(dimension, Type, variance) %>%
          pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = variance) %>%
          transmute(dimension, partition_ratio = AI / Human),
        by = "dimension")
    cat("\nBetween-participant ratio, AI over Human: the registered test",
        "(7.8.2) beside the per-arm partition (7.8.1)\n")
    print(as.data.frame(h4_ratio_compare %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))))
  }

  # One arm's three components as a named vector: image, participant,
  # remainder.
  components_for <- function(dim_name, arm) {
    v <- h4_vc_use %>% filter(dimension == dim_name, Type == arm)
    c(image       = v$variance[v$component == "between images"],
      participant = v$variance[v$component == "between participants"],
      remainder   = v$variance[v$component == "person-by-image remainder"])
  }

  # ---- The design frame: 111 participants x 10 images ----------------------
  # Integer indices are taken before id and stimulus_id become factors, so
  # that the random draws below are matched to rows by position.
  h4_frame <- expand_grid(id          = seq_len(H4_RES_N_HUMAN + H4_RES_N_AI),
                          stimulus_id = seq_len(H4_RES_N_IMAGES)) %>%
    mutate(
      Type = factor(if_else(id <= H4_RES_N_HUMAN, "Human", "AI"),
                    levels = c("Human", "AI")),
      stimulus_type = factor(if_else(stimulus_id <= H4_RES_N_IMAGES / 2,
                                     "NonFigure", "Figure"),
                             levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure")),
      Human_indicator = as.numeric(Type == "Human"),
      AI_indicator    = as.numeric(Type == "AI")
    )
  h4_id_index  <- h4_frame$id
  h4_img_index <- h4_frame$stimulus_id
  h4_is_human  <- h4_frame$Type == "Human"
  h4_frame <- h4_frame %>%
    mutate(id = factor(id), stimulus_id = factor(stimulus_id))
  stopifnot(nrow(h4_frame) == (H4_RES_N_HUMAN + H4_RES_N_AI) * H4_RES_N_IMAGES,
            sum(h4_frame$Type == "Human") == H4_RES_N_HUMAN * H4_RES_N_IMAGES,
            sum(h4_frame$Type == "AI")    == H4_RES_N_AI    * H4_RES_N_IMAGES)

  # ---- One simulated set of ratings ----------------------------------------
  # vc_human and vc_ai are the named triples from components_for(). Each row
  # takes the standard deviation of its own arm for the participant and
  # remainder draws; the image draw is shared and scaled by arm.
  simulate_ratings <- function(vc_human, vc_ai) {
    sd_by_arm <- function(component) {
      if_else(h4_is_human,
              sqrt(unname(vc_human[[component]])),
              sqrt(unname(vc_ai[[component]])))
    }
    participant_effect <- rnorm(H4_RES_N_HUMAN + H4_RES_N_AI)[h4_id_index] *
                          sd_by_arm("participant")
    image_effect       <- rnorm(H4_RES_N_IMAGES)[h4_img_index] *
                          sd_by_arm("image")
    remainder          <- rnorm(nrow(h4_frame)) * sd_by_arm("remainder")
    # Grand mean 3, the midpoint of the five-point scale; it plays no part in
    # any variance and is there only so the simulated values look like ratings.
    3 + participant_effect + image_effect + remainder
  }

  # ---- Fit both models of section 7.8.2 to one simulated dataset -----------
  # Returns one row: the two arm variances, the log ratio, the likelihood-ratio
  # statistic and p, whether the arm-specific fit was singular, whether either
  # fit raised a warning, and whether anything errored. Warnings are counted
  # and muffled rather than printed, because a thousand of them would bury
  # the output; the count is deposited.
  fit_one_h4 <- function(sim_seed, vc_human, vc_ai) {
    set.seed(sim_seed)
    d <- h4_frame
    d$rating <- simulate_ratings(vc_human, vc_ai)
    n_warn <- 0L
    result <- withCallingHandlers(
      tryCatch({
        fit_common <- lme4::lmer(
          rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
          data = d, REML = TRUE, control = H4_RES_CTRL)
        fit_byarm <- lme4::lmer(
          rating ~ Type * stimulus_type +
            (0 + Human_indicator | id) + (0 + AI_indicator | id) +
            (1 | stimulus_id),
          data = d, REML = TRUE, control = H4_RES_CTRL)
        vc   <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(fit_byarm))
        v_h  <- vc$vcov[which(vc$var1 == "Human_indicator")][1]
        v_ai <- vc$vcov[which(vc$var1 == "AI_indicator")][1]
        lrt  <- anova(fit_common, fit_byarm, refit = FALSE)
        tibble(v_human   = v_h,
               v_ai      = v_ai,
               log_ratio = log(v_ai) - log(v_h),
               lrt_chisq = lrt$Chisq[2],
               lrt_p     = lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
               singular  = lme4::isSingular(fit_byarm, tol = 1e-4),
               failed    = FALSE,
               err       = NA_character_)
      }, error = function(e) {
        tibble(v_human = NA_real_, v_ai = NA_real_, log_ratio = NA_real_,
               lrt_chisq = NA_real_, lrt_p = NA_real_, singular = NA,
               failed = TRUE, err = conditionMessage(e))
      }),
      warning = function(w) {
        n_warn <<- n_warn + 1L
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    )
    result %>% mutate(sim_seed = sim_seed, n_warnings = n_warn)
  }

  # ---- One cell: n_sim datasets at one set of true components --------------
  run_h4_cell <- function(dim_name, setting, vc_human, vc_ai, seeds) {
    sims <- map_dfr(seeds, fit_one_h4, vc_human = vc_human, vc_ai = vc_ai)
    ok   <- sims %>% filter(!failed, is.finite(log_ratio))
    n_finite <- nrow(ok)
    cell_ok  <- n_finite >= H4_RES_MIN_USED * length(seeds)
    # A cell with too few finite ratios keeps its counts and has its
    # summaries set to NA, because a spread or a rejection share computed
    # from the datasets that happened to fit is not a property of the design.
    if (!cell_ok) ok$log_ratio <- NA_real_
    reject_rate <- if (cell_ok) mean(ok$lrt_p < H4_RES_ALPHA) else NA_real_
    q_log <- if (cell_ok) quantile(ok$log_ratio, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE)
             else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    tibble(
      dimension                  = dim_name,
      setting                    = setting,
      true_var_between_Human     = unname(vc_human[["participant"]]),
      true_var_between_AI        = unname(vc_ai[["participant"]]),
      true_ratio_between         = round(unname(vc_ai[["participant"]] /
                                                vc_human[["participant"]]), 6),
      true_var_image_Human       = unname(vc_human[["image"]]),
      true_var_image_AI          = unname(vc_ai[["image"]]),
      true_var_remainder_Human   = unname(vc_human[["remainder"]]),
      true_var_remainder_AI      = unname(vc_ai[["remainder"]]),
      n_participants_Human       = H4_RES_N_HUMAN,
      n_participants_AI          = H4_RES_N_AI,
      n_images                   = H4_RES_N_IMAGES,
      n_sim                      = length(seeds),
      n_used                     = nrow(ok),
      n_failed                   = sum(sims$failed),
      n_singular                 = sum(sims$singular %in% TRUE),
      n_nonfinite_ratio          = sum(!sims$failed & !is.finite(sims$log_ratio)),
      n_warnings                 = sum(sims$n_warnings),
      mean_log_ratio             = mean(ok$log_ratio),
      sd_log_ratio               = sd(ok$log_ratio),
      median_ratio               = exp(median(ok$log_ratio)),
      ratio_q025                 = exp(q_log[1]),
      ratio_q975                 = exp(q_log[2]),
      ratio_spread_95            = exp(q_log[2]) - exp(q_log[1]),
      log_ratio_spread_95        = q_log[2] - q_log[1],
      lrt_reject_rate            = reject_rate,
      lrt_reject_mc_se           = sqrt(reject_rate * (1 - reject_rate) /
                                        nrow(ok)),
      lrt_alpha                  = H4_RES_ALPHA,
      lrt_reference              = "chi-square(1) (interior null: two positive variances set equal)",
      spread_meaning             = paste0(
        "spread of the ratio estimate across simulated datasets: the 2.5th ",
        "to 97.5th percentiles of the estimated ratio over simulations; not ",
        "the width or the coverage of any confidence interval"),
      seed                       = H4_RES_SEED,
      status                     = if (cell_ok) "run" else
                                   sprintf("too few finite ratios: %d of %d",
                                           n_finite, length(seeds)),
      note                       = if (n_finite == length(seeds)) "" else
                                   sprintf("%d of %d datasets set aside (failed or non-finite ratio)",
                                           length(seeds) - n_finite, length(seeds))
    )
  }

  # ---- The cells, in a fixed order, each with its own block of seeds -------
  h4_cells <- bind_rows(
    expand_grid(dimension = H4_RES_DIMS, setting = "null_pooled",
                true_ratio = NA_real_),
    expand_grid(dimension = H4_RES_DIMS, setting = "observed",
                true_ratio = NA_real_),
    expand_grid(dimension = H4_RES_DIMS, setting = "grid",
                true_ratio = H4_RES_RATIO_GRID)
  )
  set.seed(H4_RES_SEED)
  h4_seed_pool <- sample.int(.Machine$integer.max,
                             size = nrow(h4_cells) * H4_RES_NSIM)
  stopifnot(!any(duplicated(h4_seed_pool)))

  h4_t0 <- Sys.time()
  h4_resolution <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(h4_cells)), function(k) {
    cell     <- h4_cells[k, ]
    vc_human <- components_for(cell$dimension, "Human")
    vc_ai    <- components_for(cell$dimension, "AI")
    if (cell$setting == "null_pooled") {
      pooled <- (H4_RES_N_HUMAN * vc_human[["participant"]] +
                 H4_RES_N_AI    * vc_ai[["participant"]]) /
                (H4_RES_N_HUMAN + H4_RES_N_AI)
      vc_human[["participant"]] <- pooled
      vc_ai[["participant"]]    <- pooled
    } else if (cell$setting == "grid") {
      vc_ai[["participant"]] <- cell$true_ratio * vc_human[["participant"]]
    }
    seeds <- h4_seed_pool[((k - 1) * H4_RES_NSIM + 1):(k * H4_RES_NSIM)]
    cat(sprintf("H4 resolution: %-10s %-12s true ratio %.3f ... ",
                cell$dimension, cell$setting,
                vc_ai[["participant"]] / vc_human[["participant"]]))
    row <- run_h4_cell(cell$dimension, cell$setting, vc_human, vc_ai, seeds)
    cat(sprintf("done (%d used, %d singular, %d failed)\n",
                row$n_used, row$n_singular, row$n_failed))
    row
  })
  h4_elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), h4_t0, units = "mins"))
  cat(sprintf("H4 resolution simulation: %d cells x %d datasets in %.1f minutes\n",
              nrow(h4_cells), H4_RES_NSIM, h4_elapsed))

  # Smallest grid ratio at which the rejection share reaches the target, per
  # dimension, from the grid cells that completed. A grid that does not
  # reach it raises a warning rather than an error; the remedy is to extend
  # H4_RES_RATIO_GRID, not to read past the warning.
  h4_power_80 <- h4_resolution %>%
    filter(setting == "grid", status == "run") %>%
    group_by(dimension) %>%
    summarise(
      max_reject_in_grid           = max(lrt_reject_rate),
      smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct = if (any(lrt_reject_rate >= H4_RES_POWER_TARGET))
        min(true_ratio_between[lrt_reject_rate >= H4_RES_POWER_TARGET]) else NA_real_,
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  if (any(is.na(h4_power_80$smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct))) {
    warning("H4 resolution grid does not reach ", H4_RES_POWER_TARGET,
            " rejection for: ",
            paste(h4_power_80$dimension[is.na(h4_power_80$smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct)],
                  collapse = "; "),
            ". Extend H4_RES_RATIO_GRID.")
  }
  h4_resolution <- h4_resolution %>%
    left_join(h4_power_80 %>%
                dplyr::select(dimension, smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct),
              by = "dimension") %>%
    mutate(runtime_minutes_all_cells = h4_elapsed)

  # Every cell ran from components that exist, so an empty or half-filled
  # table is a bug rather than a missing input. A cell in which too many
  # datasets were set aside carries that in its status column, with NA
  # summaries, and a warning is printed.
  h4_done <- h4_resolution %>% filter(status == "run")
  stopifnot(
    nrow(h4_resolution) == nrow(h4_cells),
    !anyNA(h4_done$sd_log_ratio),
    !anyNA(h4_done$lrt_reject_rate)
  )
  if (nrow(h4_done) < nrow(h4_resolution)) {
    warning("H4 resolution: ", nrow(h4_resolution) - nrow(h4_done),
            " cells had too few finite ratios; their summaries are NA.")
  }

  cat("\n=== H4 resolution: the spread of the between-participant ratio estimate across simulated datasets ===\n")
  print(as.data.frame(h4_resolution %>%
    dplyr::select(dimension, setting, true_ratio_between, median_ratio,
                  sd_log_ratio, ratio_q025, ratio_q975, ratio_spread_95,
                  lrt_reject_rate, lrt_reject_mc_se, n_singular, n_failed,
                  status) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3)))))
  cat("\nSmallest grid ratio at which the likelihood-ratio test reaches",
      H4_RES_POWER_TARGET, "rejection:\n")
  print(as.data.frame(h4_power_80))
}

h4_computed_at <- Sys.time()
```

```{r h4-resolution-write}
# Written on every run, from the results above whether they were computed in
# this run or restored from the knitr cache; the run record says which. The
# skipped ledger is written the same way.
log_knitr_cache("h4-resolution", h4_computed_at)
if (all(h4_resolution$status == "skipped")) {
  log_record("fit", "H4 resolution simulation", "skipped",
             h4_resolution$note[1])
} else {
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(h4_resolution))) {
    r <- h4_resolution[k, ]
    log_record("fit", sprintf("H4 resolution, %s, %s, true ratio %.3f",
                              r$dimension, r$setting, r$true_ratio_between),
               if (r$status == "run") "ok" else "error",
               sprintf("%d of %d datasets used; %d singular, %d failed",
                       r$n_used, r$n_sim, r$n_singular, r$n_failed))
  }
}
write_output(h4_resolution, h4_resolution_path)
```

**What to look at.** Read the `null_pooled` rows first. Their `ratio_q025`
and `ratio_q975` bracket a true ratio of 1, and the distance between them is
the spread of the ratio estimate across simulated datasets when the arms
truly share one variance: how far an estimate from a sample of this size can
land from 1 by chance alone. The `lrt_reject_rate` on those rows is the
false-positive rate of the test and should sit near .05. Then read the
`observed` rows. Their spread is the spread of the estimate at the ratio the
per-arm partition of section 7.8.1 gives (its `true_ratio_between`, which
differs from the registered test's estimate for the reason given at the head
of the chunk), and their rejection rate is the power the design has against a
ratio of that size. The `grid` rows and `smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct` say
which ratios this design could have detected at 80 per cent power. If the
observed ratio on a dimension falls below that value, a null on H4 there is
uninformative rather than evidence of absence, and the manuscript should say
so in those words. None of these numbers is the width or the coverage of a
confidence interval. The interval on the ratio is computed on the real data
in `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd` by resampling participants. The spread here
describes how variable the ratio estimate is at this sample size, which is
the precision the preregistration asks about, and the manuscript should name
it as that spread and not as an expected interval width.

---

# 5. Covariate robustness

```{r covariate-robustness}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refit the primary LMMs with demographic covariates added as fixed effects.
# Random assignment means the H1 contrast should barely shift; the refit
# shows whether it does. The table carries the H1 contrast as its own row
# (emmeans, as in section 1), the TypeAI coefficient labelled as the
# non-figurative simple effect, and the fit's status on every row.
#
# Covariates: Age (centred), Gender (rare levels collapsed), Experience
# (scored 0 to 4). The response-length covariate is section 5.1.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Gender is collapsed to female, male and other, so that no level is too
# sparse to estimate.
long_cov <- long %>%
  mutate(
    gender3 = case_when(
      Gender == "Female" ~ "female",
      Gender == "Male"   ~ "male",
      TRUE               ~ "other"
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("female", "male", "other")),
    exp_num = case_when(
      Experience == "No formal training or experience"             ~ 0,
      Experience == "A little formal training or experience"       ~ 1,
      Experience == "Moderate formal training or experience"       ~ 2,
      Experience == "Extensive formal training or experience"      ~ 3,
      Experience == "Very extensive formal training or experience" ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    age_c = as.numeric(scale(Age, scale = FALSE))
  )

cov_data <- function(dim_name) {
  long_cov %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating),
           !is.na(exp_num), !is.na(age_c))
}
fit_with_covs <- function(dim_name) {
  lmerTest::lmer(
    rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + age_c + gender3 + exp_num +
             (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data = cov_data(dim_name), REML = TRUE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )
}

cov_creat <- fit_safely(fit_with_covs("creativity"))
cov_eff   <- fit_safely(fit_with_covs("effort"))

cov_summary <- bind_rows(
  tidy_with_h1(cov_creat, "creativity", "covariates (section 5), creativity",
               cov_data("creativity")),
  tidy_with_h1(cov_eff,   "effort",     "covariates (section 5), effort",
               cov_data("effort"))
) %>% relocate(dimension) %>%
  # BH p_adj within dimension over the fixed-effect family (intercept and
  # H1 row excluded), the descriptive false-discovery-rate column described
  # in §1. The H1 contrast is the quantity of interest; the covariate
  # p-values are exploratory. is_singular, convergence_note and fit_status
  # (from §1) record what the hidden warnings would have said about each fit.
  add_p_adj(p_col = "p.value", within = "dimension")

cov_summary

write_output(cov_summary,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_covariate_robustness.csv"))
summarise_lmm_table(cov_summary, "covariates: age, gender, experience",
                    "section 5",
                    "rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + age_c + gender3 + exp_num + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)")
```

## 5.1 Length-as-covariate

```{r length-covariate}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add the word count of the justification as a fixed-effect covariate. The
# justification is written after the rating, so n_words is post-treatment:
# it is measured after the manipulation, and condition could itself have
# changed it. Conditioning on it shows how the H1 contrast moves when length
# is held fixed. It cannot rule out the "maybe AI-condition participants
# just wrote less" explanation, and it cannot establish any causal path. The
# comparison of length between the arms in §6 is the direct check on that
# explanation. n_words is centred (its mean subtracted, so that zero on the
# covariate is an average-length response), which makes the Intercept and
# Type coefficients readable at average length rather than at a response of
# no words at all.
#
# The chunk runs only when the text measures were loaded in §1; the gate is
# an if() inside the chunk so that a purled copy carries it too.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!is.null(nlp)) {

long_len <- long %>%
  left_join(
    nlp %>% dplyr::select(id, stimulus_id, dimension, n_words),
    by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) %>%
  mutate(n_words_c = as.numeric(scale(n_words, scale = FALSE)))
stopifnot(nrow(long_len) == nrow(long))

len_data <- function(dim_name) {
  long_len %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating), !is.na(n_words_c))
}
fit_with_length <- function(dim_name) {
  lmerTest::lmer(
    rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + n_words_c +
             (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data = len_data(dim_name), REML = TRUE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )
}

len_creat <- fit_safely(fit_with_length("creativity"))
len_eff   <- fit_safely(fit_with_length("effort"))

len_summary <- bind_rows(
  tidy_with_h1(len_creat, "creativity", "length covariate (section 5.1), creativity",
               len_data("creativity")),
  tidy_with_h1(len_eff,   "effort",     "length covariate (section 5.1), effort",
               len_data("effort"))
) %>% relocate(dimension) %>%
