```{r length-covariate}
  # BH p_adj within dimension (descriptive, as in §1); is_singular,
  # convergence_note and fit_status as in §5.
  add_p_adj(p_col = "p.value", within = "dimension")

len_summary

write_output(len_summary,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_length_covariate.csv"))
summarise_lmm_table(len_summary, "length covariate (post-treatment; descriptive)",
                    "section 5.1",
                    "rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + n_words_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)")

} else {
  cat("Text measures not loaded; the length covariate is skipped.\n")
}
```

# 6. Non-response / engagement check

```{r engagement-check}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Context from the Qualtrics survey (Final_-_AI_Copyright_-_Study_1.qsf):
# the survey flow shows each participant ten creativity justification fields
# and ten effort justification fields (five figurative and five
# non-figurative images on each question), and every one of them has
# ForceResponse = "ON" and ForceResponseType = "ON" in its Validation
# settings, with no content validation (validation Type "None"). Qualtrics'
# ForceResponse validator stops a respondent from advancing past a page
# while a required field is empty. It does not stop a respondent from
# leaving the survey, and the exclusion flow of Study1_01_Quant.Rmd drops
# three unfinished records; and it sets no minimum length, so a single
# character satisfies it.
#
# Three consequences follow for reading engagement:
#
# 1. Among finished records, the share of non-empty justifications is at
#    the ceiling (~100%) in both conditions BY DESIGN, not by observation.
#    An AI-vs-Human comparison of that share is therefore uninformative:
#    the survey required an answer in every field.
#
# 2. The "AI-condition participants bailed out more" explanation is not
#    addressed by this check. Quitting was possible; whether it differed by
#    arm is the attrition comparison of Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 3
#    (tables/study1_attrition_by_condition.csv), not anything computed
#    here. What forced response does give this notebook is a complete set of
#    justifications for every retained participant, with no missing text to
#    impute.
#
# 3. A participant can satisfy the validator with a very short or empty-in-
#    content answer ("a", "idk"). The thresholds below, three characters and
#    three words, are thresholds this notebook applies, not ones the survey
#    enforced, and the sensitivity refit excludes participants by a
#    content-length threshold rather than a response-rate threshold.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The word count comes from the text measures (already in `nlp`). Words are
# used rather than characters because a three-character response like "yes"
# and an eighty-character response like "this is a very detailed and
# thoughtful..." differ in content in a way character counts blur.
if (is.null(nlp)) {
  cat("Text measures not loaded; skipping the length-based engagement check.\n")
  engagement <- NULL
  engagement_summary <- NULL
} else {
  resp_lengths <- long %>%
    left_join(
      nlp %>% dplyr::select(id, stimulus_id, dimension, n_words),
      by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"),
      relationship = "one-to-one"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      has_text  = nchar(response_text %>% replace_na("")) >= 3,
      has_content = !is.na(n_words) & n_words >= 3  # content-length threshold
    )
  stopifnot(nrow(resp_lengths) == nrow(long))

  engagement <- resp_lengths %>%
    group_by(id, Type) %>%
    summarise(
      n_total    = n(),
      n_any_text = sum(has_text,    na.rm = TRUE),
      n_content  = sum(has_content, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_any    = 100 * n_any_text / n_total,
      pct_content= 100 * n_content  / n_total,
      mean_words = mean(n_words,  na.rm = TRUE),
      median_words = median(n_words, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups    = "drop"
    )

  cat("=== Engagement by condition: two measures ===\n")
  cat("(a) Any response (>=3 chars). ForceResponse required a non-empty answer, not this length:\n")
  eng_any_sd_hum <- sd(engagement$pct_any[engagement$Type == "Human"])
  eng_any_sd_ai  <- sd(engagement$pct_any[engagement$Type == "AI"])
  cat(sprintf("    Human mean = %.2f%% (SD = %.3f)\n",
              mean(engagement$pct_any[engagement$Type == "Human"]),
              eng_any_sd_hum))
  cat(sprintf("    AI    mean = %.2f%% (SD = %.3f)\n",
              mean(engagement$pct_any[engagement$Type == "AI"]),
              eng_any_sd_ai))
  cat("    (Expected near the ceiling, because every field required an answer; not informative.)\n\n")

  cat("(b) Contentful response (>=3 words). ForceResponse does not enforce this:\n")
  cat(sprintf("    Human mean = %.2f%% (SD = %.3f)\n",
              mean(engagement$pct_content[engagement$Type == "Human"]),
              sd(engagement$pct_content[engagement$Type == "Human"])))
  cat(sprintf("    AI    mean = %.2f%% (SD = %.3f)\n",
              mean(engagement$pct_content[engagement$Type == "AI"]),
              sd(engagement$pct_content[engagement$Type == "AI"])))

  # Welch t-test (a t-test that does not assume equal variances in the two
  # arms) on the share of contentful responses. Unlike the any-text share,
  # this share varies across participants.
  if (sd(engagement$pct_content) > 1e-8) {
    eng_test <- t.test(pct_content ~ Type, data = engagement)
    eng_d    <- effectsize::cohens_d(pct_content ~ Type, data = engagement)
    cat("\n=== Welch t-test on contentful-response rate ===\n")
    print(eng_test)
    print(eng_d)
    eng_stat_t  <- eng_test$statistic
    eng_stat_df <- eng_test$parameter
    eng_stat_p  <- eng_test$p.value
    eng_stat_d  <- eng_d$Cohens_d
  } else {
    eng_stat_t <- eng_stat_df <- eng_stat_p <- eng_stat_d <- NA_real_
  }

  # The word-count distribution by condition, a continuous engagement
  # measure that needs no threshold.
  cat("\n=== Mean response length (words) by condition ===\n")
  words_by_type <- resp_lengths %>%
    filter(!is.na(n_words)) %>%
    group_by(Type, dimension) %>%
    summarise(mean_words = mean(n_words),
              median_words = median(n_words),
              sd_words = sd(n_words),
              .groups = "drop")
  print(words_by_type)

  # Sensitivity check: refit the primary LMMs without the participants whose
  # responses are very short. The threshold is a median response below 3
  # words, which means at least half of a participant's 20 responses ran to
  # fewer than three words, such as "idk" or "ok". The threshold is meant to
  # catch participants who put in minimal effort.
  ids_short <- engagement$id[engagement$median_words < 3]

  cat(sprintf("\nParticipants with median response length < 3 words: %d of %d\n",
              length(ids_short), nrow(engagement)))

  # Both branches give the table of section 5's shape: the H1 contrast as
  # its own row, the TypeAI simple effect labelled, the fit status on every
  # row.
  if (length(ids_short) == 0) {
    cat("No participants below threshold; primary fits stand as reported.\n")
    trim_sample <- "full sample (no short-response participants to exclude)"
    engagement_summary <- bind_rows(
      tidy_with_h1(list(fit = creat_fit), "creativity",
                   "engagement refit (section 6), creativity: primary fit",
                   long %>% filter(dimension == "creativity")),
      tidy_with_h1(list(fit = eff_fit), "effort",
                   "engagement refit (section 6), effort: primary fit",
                   long %>% filter(dimension == "effort"))
    ) %>% mutate(sample = trim_sample) %>% relocate(dimension, sample)
  } else {
    long_trimmed <- long %>% filter(!id %in% ids_short)

    trim_data <- function(dim_name) {
      long_trimmed %>%
        filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
        mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = c("Human", "AI")))
    }
    fit_trimmed <- function(dim_name) {
      lmerTest::lmer(
        rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
        data = trim_data(dim_name), REML = TRUE,
        control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
      )
    }

    trim_creat <- fit_safely(fit_trimmed("creativity"))
    trim_eff   <- fit_safely(fit_trimmed("effort"))

    trim_sample <- sprintf("excluding %d short-response pts (<3 median words)",
                           length(ids_short))
    engagement_summary <- bind_rows(
      tidy_with_h1(trim_creat, "creativity",
                   "engagement refit (section 6), creativity",
                   trim_data("creativity")),
      tidy_with_h1(trim_eff, "effort",
                   "engagement refit (section 6), effort",
                   trim_data("effort"))
    ) %>% mutate(sample = trim_sample) %>% relocate(dimension, sample)

    cat("\n=== Primary LMM refit, excluding short-response participants ===\n")
    print(engagement_summary %>% filter(term %in% c("TypeAI", H1_TERM)) %>%
            dplyr::select(dimension, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low,
                          conf.high, p.value, fit_status))
  }

  # Write the three engagement tables.
  engagement_by_condition <- tibble(
    quantity = c("Human mean % any-text",
                 "AI mean % any-text",
                 "Human mean % contentful",
                 "AI mean % contentful",
                 "Welch t (contentful %)",
                 "df", "p", "Cohen's d",
                 "N excluded at median<3 words"),
    value = c(
      round(mean(engagement$pct_any[engagement$Type == "Human"]), 3),
      round(mean(engagement$pct_any[engagement$Type == "AI"]), 3),
      round(mean(engagement$pct_content[engagement$Type == "Human"]), 3),
      round(mean(engagement$pct_content[engagement$Type == "AI"]), 3),
      round(eng_stat_t, 3),
      round(eng_stat_df, 2),
      signif(eng_stat_p, 3),
      round(eng_stat_d, 3),
      length(ids_short)
    )
  )

  # BH p_adj within dimension (descriptive, as in §1). Both branches above
  # carry is_singular, convergence_note and fit_status, as in §5.
  engagement_summary <- add_p_adj(engagement_summary, p_col = "p.value",
                                  within = "dimension")

  write_output(engagement_by_condition,
               file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_engagement_by_condition.csv"))
  write_output(engagement_summary,
               file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_engagement_trimmed_fits.csv"))
  write_output(engagement,
               file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_engagement_per_participant.csv"))
  summarise_lmm_table(engagement_summary,
                      paste0("engagement refit: ", trim_sample),
                      "section 6",
                      "rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)")
}
```

# 7. Stimulus-as-fixed sensitivity

```{r stim-as-fixed}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Judd, Westfall, & Kenny (2012): stimuli should be treated as random to
# generalize beyond the specific images used. Some reviewers ask to see the
# analysis with stimulus as fixed, which treats each image as a blocking
# factor: a category whose own mean is estimated and removed from every
# rating of that image. This refit conditions on the ten images that were
# shown: it says how the attribution estimate behaves when the differences
# among those ten images are absorbed as fixed blocks. It does
# not speak to generalization to new images, which is the question the
# random-image model of the primary analysis is built to answer.
#
# The model has no attribution-by-image-kind interaction, and every
# participant rated all ten images, five of each kind, so its TypeAI
# coefficient is already the attribution difference averaged over the ten
# images, which is the same as averaging over the two image kinds. The H1
# row is therefore that coefficient with its sign reversed (Human minus AI),
# its interval reversed with it and its p-value unchanged, and the estimand
# column says so; emmeans, averaging over the ten images, is checked to give
# the same estimate.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

stim_fx_data <- function(dim_name) {
  long %>% filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = c("Human", "AI")))
}
fit_stim_fixed <- function(dim_name) {
  # Stimulus enters as fixed (no random intercept); participant remains random.
  lmerTest::lmer(
    rating ~ Type + stimulus_id + (1 | id),
    data = stim_fx_data(dim_name), REML = TRUE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )
}

ESTIMAND_STIM_FIXED_TYPEAI <- paste0(
  "AI minus Human averaged over the ten images: with no interaction in ",
  "the model this coefficient is the attribution difference averaged over ",
  "image kind")
ESTIMAND_STIM_FIXED_H1 <- paste0(
  "H1: Human minus AI, averaged with equal weight over the two image kinds; ",
  "in this model it is the TypeAI coefficient with its sign reversed")

stim_fixed_rows <- function(res, dim_name) {
  label <- paste0("stimulus as fixed (section 7), ", dim_name)
  if (is.null(res$fit)) {
    log_record("fit", label, "error", res$error)
    return(error_row(dim_name, ESTIMAND_STIM_FIXED_H1, res$error))
  }
  fit    <- res$fit
  status <- lmm_fit_status(fit)
  ty <- broom.mixed::tidy(fit, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "TypeAI")
  h1_emm <- h1_contrast_freq(fit, stim_fx_data(dim_name))
  stopifnot(abs(h1_emm$estimate + ty$estimate) < 1e-6)
  h1 <- ty %>%
    mutate(effect    = "TypeAI coefficient, sign reversed",
           term      = H1_TERM,
           estimate  = -estimate,
           statistic = -statistic,
           conf.low  = -ty$conf.high,
           conf.high = -ty$conf.low)
  tab <- bind_rows(ty, h1) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim_name,
           estimand  = c(ESTIMAND_STIM_FIXED_TYPEAI, ESTIMAND_STIM_FIXED_H1),
           scale     = "rating points") %>%
    add_lmm_convergence(fit) %>%
    mutate(fit_status = status)
  if (!status %in% USABLE_STATUS) {
    tab <- tab %>%
      mutate(across(c(statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high), ~ NA_real_))
  }
  log_record("fit", label, status, tab$convergence_note[1])
  tab
}

stim_fx_creat <- fit_safely(fit_stim_fixed("creativity"))
stim_fx_eff   <- fit_safely(fit_stim_fixed("effort"))

stim_fx_summary <- bind_rows(
  stim_fixed_rows(stim_fx_creat, "creativity"),
  stim_fixed_rows(stim_fx_eff,   "effort")
) %>% relocate(dimension) %>%
  # p_adj column for consistency with the policy in §1. One test per
  # dimension (the H1 row restates the TypeAI row and is left out of the
  # family), so p_adj == p.value on the TypeAI row; the column exists so
  # every saved table has the same shape. is_singular, convergence_note and
  # fit_status as in §5.
  add_p_adj(p_col = "p.value", within = "dimension")

stim_fx_summary

write_output(stim_fx_summary,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_stimulus_as_fixed.csv"))

for (dm in c("creativity", "effort")) {
  h  <- stim_fx_summary %>% filter(dimension == dm, term == H1_TERM)
  ty <- stim_fx_summary %>% filter(dimension == dm, term == "TypeAI")
  add_h1_summary(
    check = "stimulus as fixed (conditions on the ten images)",
    section = "section 7", dimension = dm,
    model = "rating ~ Type + stimulus_id + (1 | id)",
    scale = "rating points",
    estimate = h$estimate %||% NA_real_, se = h$std.error %||% NA_real_,
    df = h$df %||% NA_real_,
    interval = "95% confidence interval (t, Satterthwaite df, as broom.mixed reports it)",
    ci_lo = h$conf.low %||% NA_real_, ci_hi = h$conf.high %||% NA_real_,
    p = h$p.value %||% NA_real_,
    contrast_method = "TypeAI coefficient with its sign reversed (no interaction in the model)",
    typeai_estimate = if (nrow(ty)) ty$estimate else NA_real_,
    typeai_ci_lo    = if (nrow(ty)) ty$conf.low else NA_real_,
    typeai_ci_hi    = if (nrow(ty)) ty$conf.high else NA_real_,
    fit_status = h$fit_status)
}
```

# 8. Specification curve (multiverse)

```{r specification-curve-v2, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=file_sha256(c(file.path(PATH_OUT, "study1_long_with_text.csv"), file.path(PATH_OUT_NLP, "study1_text_measures.csv")))}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Re-estimate the H1 contrast across the UNIQUE EFFECTIVE combinations of
# reasonable analytic choices:
#
#   - random effects: {intercepts_only, maximal}   (LMM and CLMM only)
#   - inference:      {LMM, CLMM, GEE} at trial level;
#                     OLS with cluster-robust SEs at participant level
#   - covariates:     {none, demographics, demog+length}
#
# The families: LMM is the linear mixed model of the primary analysis; CLMM,
# the cumulative link mixed model, treats the five ratings as ordered
# categories; GEE, generalized estimating equations, corrects its standard
# errors for the correlation among one participant's ratings instead of
# modelling participant baselines; OLS, ordinary least squares, is fitted to
# participant means.
#
# The full cross of dimension x random_fx x inference x covariates x
# aggregation has 72 cells, but two of those factors are inert in some
# branches: the participant-level branch fits one OLS per covariate set and
# consults neither inference nor random_fx, and GEE has no random-effects
# term. Counting cells would therefore overstate the number of distinct
# fits. How the grid and its columns are built:
#   1. DEDUPLICATION. Specs are keyed on their EFFECTIVE choices: at
#      participant level inference := "OLS_clusterSE" and random_fx :=
#      "n/a"; for GEE random_fx := "n/a". distinct() then yields 36 unique
#      specs (18 per dimension: LMM 2x3, CLMM 2x3, GEE 3, OLS 3), and
#      n_unique_specs is printed and asserted. The four grid columns are
#      KEPT, holding the effective values, so downstream consumers of
#      study1_specification_curve.csv find them; `analysis`
#      (aggregation-inference) is there for plotting.
#   2. SCALE column: "rating" for LMM/GEE/OLS, "logit" for CLMM. §8.1 facets
#      by it so log-odds and rating points are never sorted on one axis.
#   3. THE ESTIMATE. Every spec carries the interaction Type * stimulus_type,
#      so `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `ci_lo`, `ci_hi` and `p` are the H1
#      contrast, Human minus AI averaged over image kind, from
#      h1_contrast_freq() of section 1: emmeans on the fit, with the
#      reference distribution of each family (t on Kenward-Roger df for the
#      LMM, the normal for the CLMM and the GEE, t on G - 1 df with the
#      cluster-robust covariance for the participant-level OLS). A positive
#      estimate means the AI arm rated lower. The TypeAI coefficient, the
#      AI-minus-Human simple effect at the non-figurative images, is kept
#      beside it as `typeai_estimate`, `typeai_ci_lo`, `typeai_ci_hi` and
#      `typeai_p` for comparison.
#   4. STATUS, one of ok, singular, not_converged, error or skipped:
#      not_converged for an LMM by lmm_fit_status() (section 1), for a CLMM
#      when its optimizer returned a nonzero code, a warning mentioned
#      convergence or the Hessian, or a standard error came back NA (an
#      unusable Hessian, the matrix of second derivatives the standard
#      errors come from), and for a GEE when geepack reported an error code;
#      singular for an LMM on the boundary of its parameter space. In the
#      maximal LMM, (1 + stimulus_type | id), a singular fit can be a
#      correlation at plus or minus one with a nonzero slope variance, so
#      `is_singular` (LMM only; NA otherwise) says the structure is richer
#      than the data support, not that the slope variance is zero.
#      `converged` is TRUE for ok and singular; a not_converged spec keeps
#      its estimate and standard error for inspection, with interval and p
#      set to NA, and is left out of every count and of the plot.
#   5. NA handling. geeglm na.omit()s the model frame but receives the
#      full-length id vector, so any NA covariate value would make every
#      GEE-with-covariates spec fail with "nrow(zsca) and length(y) not
#      match". As a general safeguard, ALL families therefore use an
#      identical NA-free analysis set (drop_na on every covariate used),
#      whether or not the deposited data contain a missing value, plus
#      arrange(id) because geepack requires clusters to be contiguous.
#      With the same rows, comparisons between families are like for like.
#   6. FAILURE LEDGER written to tables/study1_specification_curve_failures.csv
#      (every spec whose status is not ok or singular, with its message; a
#      0-row file is written when nothing fails) and printed, with attempted
#      / converged / singular / not converged / sign-flip counts.
#   7. Participant-level branch: lm() on two rows per participant (Figure /
#      NonFigure means), whose SEs come from sandwich::vcovCL(cluster = id)
#      with a t(G-1) reference, G being the number of participants. These
#      are cluster-robust SEs (standard errors that allow the two rows from
#      one participant to be correlated; HC1 applies the G/(G-1)
#      small-sample adjustment). The point estimate is the plain lm() one.
#   8. Exclusion strictness is NOT one of the factors varied here, and the
#      curve should not be described as though it were: the excluded rows
#      are not in study1_long_with_text.csv, so varying them would require
#      Study1_01_Quant.Rmd to write a permissive set first.
#
# INTERPRETATION NOTE. "All estimates on the same side of zero" is a
# DESCRIPTIVE statement about this grid. It is not a Simonsohn et al.
# (2020) inferential specification-curve test (that needs the permutation
# / bootstrap-under-the-null step, which is not run here). Say "the sign
# and significance of the H1 contrast did not depend on any analytic
# choice we varied", not "strong evidence".
#
# The chunk is cached, and cache.extra keys the cache on the SHA-256
# checksums of the long data and of the text measures, the two files the
# specifications are fitted to. The tables are written by the uncached
# chunk that follows.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Stop if a package the specifications need is missing, rather than
# dropping those specifications.
if (!requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package 'sandwich' is required for cluster-robust SEs in the ",
       "participant-level specifications. install.packages('sandwich').")
}
if (!requireNamespace("geepack", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package 'geepack' is required for the GEE specifications. ",
       "install.packages('geepack').")
}

grid_full <- expand.grid(
  dimension    = c("creativity", "effort"),
  random_fx    = c("intercepts_only", "maximal"),
  inference    = c("LMM", "CLMM", "GEE"),
  covariates   = c("none", "demographics", "demog_length"),
  aggregation  = c("trial", "participant"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Key on EFFECTIVE choices, then deduplicate.
grid <- grid_full %>%
  mutate(
    inference = if_else(aggregation == "participant", "OLS_clusterSE", inference),
    random_fx = case_when(
      aggregation == "participant" ~ "n/a (participant-level OLS, cluster-robust SE)",
      inference == "GEE"           ~ "n/a (GEE, exchangeable working correlation)",
      TRUE                         ~ random_fx
    ),
    analysis = paste(aggregation, inference, sep = "-"),
    scale    = if_else(inference == "CLMM", "logit", "rating")
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(dimension, aggregation, inference, random_fx, covariates)

n_grid_cells   <- nrow(grid_full)
n_unique_specs <- nrow(grid)
cat(sprintf("Crossed grid: %d cells -> %d unique effective specifications (%d per dimension)\n",
            n_grid_cells, n_unique_specs, n_unique_specs / 2))
# Per dimension: LMM 2 RE x 3 cov = 6; CLMM 6; GEE 3; OLS 3 -> 18.
stopifnot(n_unique_specs == 36, !any(duplicated(grid)))

cov_vars_for <- function(cov_choice) {
  switch(cov_choice,
    none         = character(0),
    demographics = c("age_c", "gender3", "exp_num"),
    demog_length = c("age_c", "gender3", "exp_num", "n_words_c"),
    stop("unknown covariate set: ", cov_choice))
}

na_result <- function(msg, status = "error") {
  tibble(estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
         ci_lo = NA_real_, ci_hi = NA_real_, p = NA_real_,
         typeai_estimate = NA_real_, typeai_ci_lo = NA_real_,
         typeai_ci_hi = NA_real_, typeai_p = NA_real_,
         is_singular = NA, status = status, contrast_method = NA_character_,
         err = msg)
}

# One spec's row: the H1 contrast from h1_contrast_freq(), the TypeAI simple
# effect with its interval and p, the singular flag, the status and the
# method. A spec whose status is not usable keeps its estimate and standard
# error, with interval and p set to NA.
spec_row <- function(h1, typeai_est, typeai_se, typeai_crit, typeai_p,
                     is_singular, status, method, note = NA_character_) {
  usable <- status %in% USABLE_STATUS
  tibble(
    estimate        = h1$estimate,
    se              = h1$se,
    df              = h1$df,
    ci_lo           = if (usable) h1$ci_lo else NA_real_,
    ci_hi           = if (usable) h1$ci_hi else NA_real_,
    p               = if (usable) h1$p else NA_real_,
    typeai_estimate = typeai_est,
    typeai_ci_lo    = if (usable) typeai_est - typeai_crit * typeai_se else NA_real_,
    typeai_ci_hi    = if (usable) typeai_est + typeai_crit * typeai_se else NA_real_,
    typeai_p        = if (usable) typeai_p else NA_real_,
    is_singular     = is_singular,
    status          = status,
    contrast_method = method,
    err             = note
  )
}

# run_spec() fits one spec and returns its H1 contrast and its TypeAI
# coefficient. Every branch returns one spec_row() or na_result().
# as.numeric() everywhere because summary(geeglm)$coefficients is a
# data.frame (1-row indexing gives a data.frame, which breaks bind_rows).
# Warnings raised while fitting are collected rather than printed; for the
# CLMM and the GEE, a warning about convergence or the Hessian marks the
# spec not_converged, and for the LMM lme4's own record is read instead.
run_spec <- function(i) {
  spec <- grid[i, ]
  d <- long_cov %>% filter(dimension == spec$dimension, !is.na(rating))

  # Aggregation: participant x stimulus_type means (two rows per participant).
  if (spec$aggregation == "participant") {
    d <- d %>%
      group_by(id, Type, stimulus_type, gender3, exp_num, age_c) %>%
      summarise(rating = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  }

  # The length covariate requires the text measures. At participant level
  # the summarise() above has dropped `dimension` from `d`, so word counts
  # are averaged to one row per participant within the current dimension,
  # which avoids a cross-join.
  if (spec$covariates == "demog_length") {
    if (is.null(nlp)) {
      return(bind_cols(spec,
        na_result("skipped: text-measure file not found (n_words unavailable)",
                  status = "skipped")))
    }
    if (spec$aggregation == "participant") {
      nlp_part <- nlp %>%
        filter(dimension == spec$dimension, !is.na(n_words)) %>%
        group_by(id) %>%
        summarise(n_words = mean(n_words, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
      d <- d %>%
        left_join(nlp_part, by = "id", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
        mutate(n_words_c = as.numeric(scale(n_words, scale = FALSE)))
    } else {
      d <- d %>%
        left_join(
          nlp %>% dplyr::select(id, stimulus_id, dimension, n_words),
          by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"),
          relationship = "one-to-one"
        ) %>%
        mutate(n_words_c = as.numeric(scale(n_words, scale = FALSE)))
    }
  }

  cov_vars <- cov_vars_for(spec$covariates)
  cov_str  <- if (length(cov_vars)) {
    paste("+", paste(cov_vars, collapse = " + "))
  } else ""

  # Identical NA-free analysis set for every family, sorted by id (geepack
  # needs contiguous clusters and an id vector the same length as the model
  # frame).
  d <- d %>%
    tidyr::drop_na(all_of(c("rating", "Type", "stimulus_type", cov_vars))) %>%
    arrange(id) %>%
    droplevels()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(bind_cols(spec, na_result("no rows after NA filter")))

  re_str <- if (spec$aggregation == "participant" || spec$inference == "GEE") {
    ""
  } else if (spec$random_fx == "intercepts_only") {
    "+ (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)"
  } else {
    "+ (1 + stimulus_type | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)"
  }
  fx_str <- paste("rating ~ Type * stimulus_type", cov_str)
  f      <- as.formula(paste(fx_str, re_str))
  warns  <- character(0)
  collect_warning <- function(w) {
    warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
  conv_warning <- function() {
    any(grepl("converg|Hessian", warns, ignore.case = TRUE))
  }

  est <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers({
    if (spec$inference == "OLS_clusterSE") {
      fit <- lm(f, data = d)
      V   <- sandwich::vcovCL(fit, cluster = d$id)   # HC1 + G/(G-1)
      b   <- as.numeric(coef(fit)["TypeAI"])
      se  <- as.numeric(sqrt(V["TypeAI", "TypeAI"]))
      G   <- n_distinct(d$id)
      h1  <- h1_contrast_freq(fit, d, df_override = G - 1, vcov_override = V)
      spec_row(h1, b, se, qt(0.975, G - 1), 2 * pt(-abs(b / se), G - 1),
               is_singular = NA, status = "ok",
               method = paste0("emmeans on lm with the cluster-robust ",
                               "covariance (sandwich::vcovCL), t on G - 1 df"))
    } else if (spec$inference == "LMM") {
      fit <- suppressMessages(lmerTest::lmer(f, data = d, REML = TRUE,
             control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
      co  <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
      h1  <- h1_contrast_freq(fit, d)
      spec_row(h1, as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Estimate"]),
               as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Std. Error"]), 1.96,
               as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Pr(>|t|)"]),
               is_singular = lme4::isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-4),
               status = lmm_fit_status(fit),
               method = "emmeans on lmer, t on Kenward-Roger df",
               note = {
                 m <- c(unlist(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages),
                        unlist(fit@optinfo$warnings))
                 if (length(m)) paste(m, collapse = "; ") else NA_character_
               })
    } else if (spec$inference == "CLMM") {
      d2 <- d %>% mutate(rating_ord = factor(rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE))
      f2 <- as.formula(gsub("rating", "rating_ord", paste(fx_str, re_str),
                            fixed = TRUE))
      fit <- suppressMessages(ordinal::clmm(f2, data = d2, link = "logit"))
      co  <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
      se_missing <- anyNA(co[c("TypeAI", "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"),
                             "Std. Error"])
      status <- if (!identical(as.integer(fit$optRes$convergence), 0L) ||
                    se_missing || conv_warning()) "not_converged" else "ok"
      h1 <- if (se_missing) {
        tibble(estimate = -(coef(fit)[["TypeAI"]] +
                              0.5 * coef(fit)[["TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"]]),
               se = NA_real_, df = Inf, ci_lo = NA_real_, ci_hi = NA_real_,
               statistic = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
      } else h1_contrast_freq(fit, d2, df_override = Inf)
      spec_row(h1, as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Estimate"]),
               as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Std. Error"]), 1.96,
               as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Pr(>|z|)"]),
               is_singular = NA, status = status,
               method = "emmeans on clmm (latent log-odds scale), normal reference",
               note = if (status == "ok") NA_character_ else paste0(
                 "optimizer code ", fit$optRes$convergence,
                 if (se_missing) "; NA standard error (Hessian not usable)" else "",
                 if (length(warns)) paste0("; ", paste(warns, collapse = "; ")) else ""))
    } else if (spec$inference == "GEE") {
      fit <- geepack::geeglm(f, id = id, data = d, corstr = "exchangeable")
      co  <- summary(fit)$coefficients
      status <- if (!identical(as.integer(fit$geese$error), 0L) ||
                    conv_warning()) "not_converged" else "ok"
      h1 <- h1_contrast_freq(fit, d, df_override = Inf)
      spec_row(h1, as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Estimate"]),
               as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Std.err"]), 1.96,
               as.numeric(co["TypeAI", "Pr(>|W|)"]),
               is_singular = NA, status = status,
               method = "emmeans on geeglm (robust covariance), normal reference",
               note = if (status == "ok") NA_character_ else paste0(
                 "geese error code ", fit$geese$error,
                 if (length(warns)) paste0("; ", paste(warns, collapse = "; ")) else ""))
    } else {
      stop("unknown inference family: ", spec$inference)
    }
  }, warning = collect_warning),
  error = function(e) na_result(conditionMessage(e)))

  bind_cols(spec, est)
}

spec_results <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(grid)), run_spec) %>%
  mutate(
    estimand  = H1_TERM,
    converged = status %in% USABLE_STATUS,
    n_unique_specs_total = n_unique_specs
  ) %>%
  # p_adj (BH within dimension) for consistency with the policy in §1.
  # Specification p-values are NOT independent tests of distinct hypotheses
  # (they are one hypothesis under many models), so this column is
  # descriptive; do not read it as a family-wise claim. A spec that is not
  # usable has p NA and is left out of the adjustment.
  add_p_adj(p_col = "p", within = "dimension")

stopifnot(nrow(spec_results) == n_unique_specs,
          all(spec_results$status %in%
                c("ok", "singular", "not_converged", "error", "skipped")))

# ---- Failure ledger ---------------------------------------------------------
spec_failures <- spec_results %>%
  filter(!converged) %>%
  dplyr::select(dimension, analysis, aggregation, inference, random_fx,
                covariates, scale, status, err)

# ---- Counts (descriptive) ---------------------------------------------------
# Under Human minus AI the reference sign is POSITIVE (AI rated lower); a
# "sign flip" is a usable spec with estimate < 0. Every count but n_specs,
# n_failed, n_not_converged and n_skipped is taken over the usable specs
# (status ok or singular).
rng <- function(x) if (length(x)) range(x) else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
spec_counts <- spec_results %>%
  group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specs         = n(),
    n_converged     = sum(converged),
    n_not_converged = sum(status == "not_converged"),
    n_failed        = sum(status == "error"),
    n_skipped       = sum(status == "skipped"),
    n_singular      = sum(status == "singular"),
    n_sign_flips    = sum(converged & estimate < 0),
    n_sig_p05       = sum(converged & p < 0.05),
    rating_est_min  = rng(estimate[converged & scale == "rating"])[1],
    rating_est_max  = rng(estimate[converged & scale == "rating"])[2],
    logit_est_min   = rng(estimate[converged & scale == "logit"])[1],
    logit_est_max   = rng(estimate[converged & scale == "logit"])[2],
    estimand        = H1_TERM,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\n=== Specification curve: counts by dimension ===\n")
print(spec_counts, width = Inf)
cat(sprintf("\nUnique effective specifications: %d (from %d crossed grid cells)\n",
            n_unique_specs, n_grid_cells))
if (nrow(spec_failures) > 0) {
  cat("\n=== Failure / skip ledger (also written to tables/) ===\n")
  print(spec_failures, n = Inf, width = Inf)
} else {
  cat("\nNo specification failed or was skipped.\n")
}
cat("\nNOTE: 'n_sign_flips = 0' is a DESCRIPTIVE statement about this grid,",
    "not a Simonsohn et al. (2020) inferential test.\n")

spec_results

spec_computed_at <- Sys.time()
```

```{r specification-curve-write}
# Written on every run, from the results above whether they were computed in
# this run or restored from the knitr cache; the run record says which.
log_knitr_cache("specification-curve-v2", spec_computed_at)
for (k in seq_len(nrow(spec_results))) {
  r <- spec_results[k, ]
  log_record("fit", sprintf("specification curve, %s, %s, %s, %s",
                            r$dimension, r$analysis, r$random_fx,
                            r$covariates),
             r$status, coalesce(r$err, ""))
}
write_output(spec_failures,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_specification_curve_failures.csv"))
write_output(spec_counts,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_specification_curve_counts.csv"))
write_output(spec_results,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_specification_curve.csv"))
```

## 8.1 Plot the specification curve

```{r spec-curve-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two panels, in the layout of Simonsohn et al. (2020). The top panel shows
# each spec's estimate and CI, sorted by estimate; the bottom panel is a dot
# matrix of the analytic choices that produced each estimate.
#
# The curve is FACETED BY SCALE: one sorted curve per scale, side by side,
# with the unit in the y-axis label. Rating-point coefficients (LMM/GEE/OLS)
# and CLMM cumulative log-odds are never sorted on one axis, because most of
# the visible spread there would be a change of units rather than an
# analytic choice. The validity filter keeps the usable specs (converged,
# meaning status ok or singular), so a CLMM with an NA SE does not appear as
# a grey dot. Attempted / converged counts are in the subtitle so the figure
# caption can quote them. The y axis is the H1 contrast, Human minus AI
# averaged over image kind, so a point above zero is a spec in which the AI
# arm rated lower.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

plot_spec_curve <- function(data, dim_name) {
  d_all <- data %>% filter(dimension == dim_name, converged)
  n_attempted <- sum(data$dimension == dim_name)
  scales_present <- intersect(c("rating", "logit"), unique(d_all$scale))
  stopifnot(length(scales_present) >= 1)

  panels <- map(scales_present, function(sc) {
    d <- d_all %>%
      filter(scale == sc) %>%
      arrange(estimate) %>%
      mutate(spec_id = row_number(), sig = p < 0.05)

    ylab <- if (sc == "rating") {
      "H1 contrast: Human - AI, averaged over image kind (rating points)"
    } else {
      "H1 contrast: Human - AI, averaged over image kind (log-odds, CLMM)"
    }

    top <- ggplot(d, aes(x = spec_id, y = estimate)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
      geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi, color = sig),
                      size = 0.2, fatten = 1.4) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "grey60")) +
      labs(title = sprintf("%s, %s scale", dim_name, sc),
           subtitle = sprintf("%d converged specs (of %d attempted for %s)",
                              nrow(d), n_attempted, dim_name),
           x = NULL, y = ylab) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
            legend.position = "none")

    # Bottom panel: which EFFECTIVE choices produced each spec.
    choice_long <- d %>%
      dplyr::select(spec_id, analysis, random_fx, covariates) %>%
      pivot_longer(-spec_id, names_to = "choice", values_to = "value")

    bottom <- ggplot(choice_long, aes(x = spec_id, y = value)) +
      geom_point(size = 0.5) +
      facet_grid(choice ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
      theme(
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank()
      )

    top / bottom + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 3))
  })

  # Panel widths proportional to the number of specs on each scale.
  widths <- map_dbl(scales_present, ~ max(3, sum(d_all$scale == .x)))
  wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1, widths = widths)
}

fig_spec_creat <- plot_spec_curve(spec_results, "creativity")
fig_spec_eff   <- plot_spec_curve(spec_results, "effort")

fig_spec_creat
fig_spec_eff

save_figure(fig_spec_creat,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_specification_curve_creativity.pdf"),
            width = 10, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
save_figure(fig_spec_eff,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_specification_curve_effort.pdf"),
            width = 10, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
save_figure(fig_spec_creat,
            file.path(PATH_PAPER_FIG, "study1_specification_curve_creativity.pdf"),
            width = 10, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
save_figure(fig_spec_eff,
            file.path(PATH_PAPER_FIG, "study1_specification_curve_effort.pdf"),
            width = 10, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
```

## 8.2 The H1 contrast across the checks

One row per check and dimension: the H1 contrast as each check estimates it,
on its own model's scale, beside the `TypeAI` simple effect the same model
gives. The first rows are the primary fits of `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd`, the
reference every other row varies; the specification curve is summarised in
its own counts table, where `rating_est_min` and `rating_est_max` give the
range of the H1 contrast over the usable specifications.

```{r h1-contrast-summary}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Columns of tables/study1_robustness_h1_contrast.csv:
#   check, section, dimension, model, scale   which check, where it is run,
#                                             the fitted model and its scale
#                                             (rating points or log-odds).
#   estimand                                  the H1 definition, the same on
#                                             every row.
#   estimate, se, df, interval, ci_lo, ci_hi, p, pd
#                                             the H1 contrast, Human minus
#                                             AI averaged over image kind,
#                                             with the kind of interval named
#                                             in `interval`; the Bayesian rows
#                                             carry a credible interval and
#                                             the probability of direction in
#                                             place of p.
#   contrast_method                           how the contrast was computed
#                                             from that model.
#   typeai_simple_effect, typeai_ci_lo, typeai_ci_hi
#                                             the TypeAI coefficient of the
#                                             same model: AI minus Human at
#                                             the non-figurative images where
#                                             the model has the interaction,
#                                             and the averaged difference with
#                                             the opposite sign where it does
#                                             not (section 7).
#   fit_status                                ok, singular, not_converged or
#                                             error; interval and p are NA
#                                             unless the status is usable.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
h1_contrast_table <- H1_SUMMARY %>%
  mutate(across(c(estimate, se, df, ci_lo, ci_hi, p, pd,
                  typeai_simple_effect, typeai_ci_lo, typeai_ci_hi),
                as.numeric))
stopifnot(nrow(h1_contrast_table) > 0,
          all(h1_contrast_table$fit_status %in%
                c("ok", "singular", "not_converged", "error")))

print(as.data.frame(h1_contrast_table %>%
  dplyr::select(check, dimension, scale, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi, p, pd,
                typeai_simple_effect, fit_status) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

write_output(h1_contrast_table,
             file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_robustness_h1_contrast.csv"))
```

---

# 9. Summary of robustness outputs

Each check writes its own table to `tables/`, so each can be checked on its
own. The supplement may combine them into one robustness table across the
five studies. Every table that re-estimates H1 carries a row labelled
`H1 contrast: Human - AI, averaged over image kind`, an `estimand` column
naming what each attribution row estimates, a `scale` column, and a
`fit_status` column (ok, singular, not_converged or error).

**Files written to `tables/`:**

- `study1_brms_primary_fixed.csv`: Bayesian replication (§2): one row per fixed effect and one H1 row, with `estimand`, `scale`, the per-row Rhat, bulk and tail ESS, `rhat_max_all_params`, `ess_bulk_min_all_params`, `ess_tail_min_all_params`, `n_divergent`, `n_max_treedepth`, `max_treedepth` and `fit_status`
- `study1_brms_cumulative_fixed.csv`: Bayesian cumulative-ordinal version (§2.1), same columns, on the log-odds scale
- `study1_brms_prior_sensitivity.csv`: wide-prior refit beside the default (§2.2; only when `RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY = TRUE`), the H1 row among the rows compared
- `study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv`: the attribution-by-image-kind interaction tested against the wider bounds in `EQUIV_SENSITIVITY_BOUNDS`, both as two one-sided tests on each primary lmer fit and as a region of practical equivalence on each saved Gaussian brms fit (§3), with the `fit_status` of the fit each row comes from. Descriptive sensitivity only: the `role` column says so on every row, and `bound_is_registered` is FALSE throughout, because the registered bound of ±0.20 is tested in `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd` section 7.10 under both random-effects structures.
- `study1_sensitivity_power.csv`: design-sensitivity power at hypothesized betas (§4); the `TypeAI` rows are the H1 contrast, from the primary model refitted with image kind sum-coded, and the interaction rows are from the treatment-coded primary fit; columns `dimension`, `term`, `estimand`, `coding`, `hypothesized_beta_rating_units`, `implied_d_total_sd`, `implied_d_residual_sd`, `power`, `ci_lo`, `ci_hi`, `mc_se`, `nsim`, `n_sim_errors`, `analysis_type`, `status`
- `study1_sensitivity_power_80pct.csv`: smallest beta reaching 80% per dimension and term (§4), with `estimand`, `coding`, `h3_registered_bound` and a `role` column on the interaction rows saying that the smallest detectable interaction is descriptive context for H3 and carries no verdict; NA when the grid does not reach 80%
- `study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv`: the H3 half of "what the design can resolve" (§4). One row per dimension, true interaction (0 and 0.10 rating points) and bound (0.20 registered; 0.30 and 0.50 descriptive), with the power of the two one-sided tests at that bound (`equivalence_power`, its Monte Carlo standard error `mc_se` and exact binomial interval), the analytic approximation from the deposited standard error (`analytic_power`), the counts of singular, failed and warned refits, a per-cell `status`, the registered verdict read from `study1_h3_equivalence.csv` (`registered_test_passed`, `h3_claim`, `h3_structure_used`), and `h3_equivalence_informative`: TRUE on a pass, and on a fail TRUE only when the power at the registered bound under a true zero reaches 80%, NA when that cell did not complete. Carries `seed` and `runtime_minutes_all_cells`.
- `study1_h4_resolution.csv`: the H4 half of "what the design can resolve" (§4.1): one row per dimension and setting (`null_pooled`, `observed`, and the grid of true ratios 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3), with the standard deviation of the estimated log ratio across simulated datasets, the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles of the estimated ratio and the distance between them (the spread of the ratio estimate across simulated datasets, which is not the width or the coverage of any confidence interval, as the `spread_meaning` column says), the likelihood-ratio rejection share at .05 with its Monte Carlo standard error, the counts of singular, failed and non-finite fits, and `smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct`. Carries a `status` column (`run` for a completed cell); a one-row `skipped` ledger is written instead when `tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv` is absent.
- `study1_covariate_robustness.csv`: age, gender and experience added to the primary LMMs (§5), with the H1 row, `estimand`, `scale`, `is_singular`, `convergence_note`, `fit_status`, `p_adj` and `p_adj_method`
- `study1_length_covariate.csv`: response-length covariate added (§5.1), same columns
- `study1_engagement_per_participant.csv`, `study1_engagement_by_condition.csv`, `study1_engagement_trimmed_fits.csv`: engagement check (§6); the trimmed fits carry the same columns as §5
- `study1_stimulus_as_fixed.csv`: stimulus as fixed effect (§7): the TypeAI row and the H1 row, which is that coefficient with its sign reversed because the model has no interaction, with `estimand`, `scale`, `is_singular`, `convergence_note`, `fit_status`, `p_adj` and `p_adj_method`
- `study1_specification_curve.csv`: the 36 UNIQUE effective specifications (18 per dimension) (§8). `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `ci_lo`, `ci_hi` and `p` are the H1 contrast (Human minus AI, so positive means the AI arm rated lower); `typeai_estimate`, `typeai_ci_lo`, `typeai_ci_hi` and `typeai_p` are the TypeAI simple effect of the same fit; with `analysis`, `scale`, `estimand`, `contrast_method`, `is_singular`, `status` (ok, singular, not_converged, error, skipped), `converged` (TRUE for ok and singular), `n_unique_specs_total`, `p_adj` and `p_adj_method`; `random_fx` and `inference` hold the effective choices, so a participant-level row reads `OLS_clusterSE` / `n/a`
- `study1_specification_curve_failures.csv`: every specification that is not usable, with its message (§8), written even when empty
- `study1_specification_curve_counts.csv`: per dimension, the number of specs, converged, not converged, failed, skipped and singular, the sign flips (usable specs with an H1 estimate below zero), the count at p < .05, and the range of the H1 estimate on each scale (§8)
- `study1_robustness_h1_contrast.csv`: the H1 contrast from every check in one table, beside the TypeAI simple effect of the same model (§8.2)
- `study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv`: the run record (§9.1)

**Figures:**

- `figures/study1_brms_ppc.pdf`: posterior predictive checks
- `figures/study1_specification_curve_{creativity,effort}.pdf`: multiverse plots of the H1 contrast, faceted by scale (rating points | CLMM log-odds)
- Mirrored copies of the specification curves in `Docs/Writing/Final Paper/figures/`

**Models (saved, reused only after brms's `on_change` check and the settings check of §2):**

- `models/study1_brms_primary_{creativity,effort}.rds`: Bayesian Gaussian LMMs
- `models/study1_brms_cumulative_{creativity,effort}.rds`: Bayesian ordinal LMMs
- `models/study1_brms_primary_{creativity,effort}_priorwide.rds`: wide-prior refits (§2.2; only once `RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY = TRUE` has been run)

**Inputs expected from other notebooks:**

- `study1_long_with_text.csv`, `models/study1_lmm_{creativity,effort}.rds` (Study1_01_Quant); §1 stops if the two models were not fitted to the long data's rows
- `tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv` (Study1_01_Quant §7.8.1; §4.1 is skipped and writes a one-row `skipped` ledger without it)
- `tables/study1_h3_equivalence.csv` (Study1_01_Quant §7.10; without it the registered verdict is recomputed in §4 from the intercepts-only fits alone and the `verdict_source` column says so)
- `tables/study1_confirmatory_family.csv` (Study1_01_Quant §7.9; optional, read only to check that the H1 contrast recomputed here matches the one deposited there)
- `nlp/study1_text_measures.csv` (Study1_02_Text; optional: §5.1, §6 and the `demog_length` specs are skipped and recorded as not written without it; §1 stops if its keys do not match the long data one to one)

**Downstream consumers to check after re-running:** `Study1_Supplements.Rmd` reads `study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv`, the two brms tables and `study1_specification_curve.csv`, and should take a table as a result of this run only when the manifest lists it as written by this run.

## 9.1 Run manifest

The last chunk writes `tables/study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv`. Because
every output, the manifest among them, is deleted when the run starts, a
manifest on disk means the run reached its last chunk, and its rows say
which files that run wrote.

```{r run-manifest}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One row per record. The first four columns are those of
# tables/study1_quant_run_manifest.csv, so one reader can check both:
#   run_id            this run's identifier (run-record chunk).
#   file              the path, relative to this Study 1 folder, or under
#                     Docs/Writing/Final Paper/ for the paper copies; NA for
#                     a record that is not a file.
#   written_this_run  for an output, TRUE when this run wrote the file and
#                     it is on disk with the checksum recorded when it was
#                     written; FALSE otherwise. NA on rows that are not
#                     outputs.
#   sha256            the file's SHA-256 checksum, NA when it does not exist.
# and then:
#   role              what the row records: run, source, setting, input,
#                     fit, cache or output.
#   item              what the row is about: a file name, a fit, a setting.
#   status            run: complete. input: read or absent. fit: ok,
#                     singular, not_converged, error or skipped. cache:
#                     reused, refitted or fitted (a saved brms fit), restored
#                     or computed (a knitr-cached chunk). output: written or
#                     not written.
#   detail            the reason, the message or the value.
#   recorded_at       when the row was recorded.
# The manifest lists itself as an output, written.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
source_path <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
if (is.null(source_path)) {
  source_path <- file.path(PATH_ANALYSIS, "Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd")
}
log_record("source", basename(source_path),
           if (file.exists(source_path)) "read" else "absent",
           "the notebook as it stood when this run finished",
           file = manifest_label(source_path), sha256 = file_sha256(source_path))

settings <- c(
  seed_notebook          = "20260421",
  RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY  = as.character(RUN_PRIOR_SENSITIVITY),
  BRMS_FILE_REFIT        = BRMS_FILE_REFIT,
  REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND = as.character(REGISTERED_EQUIV_BOUND),
  POWER_NSIM             = as.character(POWER_NSIM),
  H3_POW_NSIM            = as.character(H3_POW_NSIM),
  H3_POW_SEED            = as.character(H3_POW_SEED),
  H4_RES_NSIM            = if (exists("H4_RES_NSIM")) as.character(H4_RES_NSIM) else NA_character_,
  H4_RES_SEED            = if (exists("H4_RES_SEED")) as.character(H4_RES_SEED) else NA_character_,
  R_version              = R.version.string,
  packages               = paste(
    sapply(c("lme4", "lmerTest", "emmeans", "brms", "simr", "ordinal",
             "geepack", "sandwich", "posterior", "pbkrtest"),
           function(p) paste0(p, " ", as.character(packageVersion(p)))),
    collapse = "; ")
)
for (nm in names(settings)) log_record("setting", nm, settings[[nm]])

# One output row per file in OUTPUT_FILES. A file counts as written by this
# run when write_output() or save_figure() recorded it and the file on disk
# still has the checksum recorded then.
written <- RUN_LOG %>% filter(role == "output") %>%
  group_by(file) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
output_rows <- tibble(path = setdiff(OUTPUT_FILES, PATH_MANIFEST)) %>%
  mutate(
    file   = manifest_label(path),
    item   = basename(path),
    sha256 = file_sha256(path),
    logged_sha256 = written$sha256[match(file, written$file)],
    written_this_run = !is.na(sha256) & !is.na(logged_sha256) &
                       sha256 == logged_sha256,
    status = if_else(written_this_run, "written", "not written"),
    detail = case_when(
      written_this_run ~ coalesce(written$detail[match(file, written$file)], ""),
      path %in% names(OUTPUT_NOTES) ~ unname(OUTPUT_NOTES[path]),
      TRUE ~ "not written by this run; see the fit and cache records")
  )

run_elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), RUN_STARTED_AT, units = "mins"))
n_bad_fits  <- sum(RUN_LOG$role == "fit" &
                     RUN_LOG$status %in% c("not_converged", "error"))
log_record("run", RUN_ID, "complete",
           sprintf(paste0("started %s; finished %s; %.1f minutes; %d outputs ",
                          "written, %d not written; %d fits not converged or ",
                          "in error"),
                   format(RUN_STARTED_AT, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                   format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), run_elapsed,
                   sum(output_rows$written_this_run),
                   sum(!output_rows$written_this_run), n_bad_fits))

run_manifest <- bind_rows(
  RUN_LOG %>% filter(role != "output"),
  output_rows %>% dplyr::select(file, item, status, detail, sha256,
                                written_this_run) %>%
    mutate(role = "output",
           recorded_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
  tibble(role = "output", file = manifest_label(PATH_MANIFEST),
         item = basename(PATH_MANIFEST), status = "written",
         detail = "this file", sha256 = NA_character_,
         written_this_run = TRUE,
         recorded_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))
) %>%
  mutate(run_id = RUN_ID) %>%
  dplyr::select(run_id, file, written_this_run, sha256, role, item,
                status, detail, recorded_at)

cat(sprintf("Run %s: %d outputs written, %d not written; %d fits not converged or in error.\n",
            RUN_ID, sum(output_rows$written_this_run),
            sum(!output_rows$written_this_run), n_bad_fits))
if (any(!output_rows$written_this_run)) {
  print(as.data.frame(output_rows %>% filter(!written_this_run) %>%
                        dplyr::select(file, detail)))
}
print(as.data.frame(run_manifest %>% filter(role %in% c("cache", "fit")) %>%
                      count(role, status)))
write_csv(run_manifest, PATH_MANIFEST)
```
